```{r}
# table formatting
fmt_tbl <- function(df, right = NULL, caption = NULL) {
  right_cols <- union(names(df)[vapply(df, is.numeric, TRUE)], right)
  left_cols <- setdiff(names(df), right_cols)
  ft <- flextable::flextable(df)
  ft <- flextable::fontsize(ft, size = 11, part = "all")
  ft <- flextable::align(ft, align = "center", part = "header")
  if (length(right_cols)) ft <- flextable::align(ft, j = right_cols, align = "right", part = "body")
  if (length(left_cols)) ft <- flextable::align(ft, j = left_cols, align = "left", part = "body")
  ft <- flextable::line_spacing(ft, space = 1, part = "all")
  ft <- flextable::padding(ft, padding.top = 1, padding.bottom = 1,part = "all")
  if (!is.null(caption)) ft <- flextable::set_caption(ft, caption)
  flextable::set_table_properties(ft, layout = "autofit", width = 1)
}

in_km <- function(x, km = "+proj=utm +zone=5 +datum=WGS84 +units=km +no_defs") {
  if (!inherits(x, "SpatRaster")) return(sf::st_transform(x, km))
  ext(x) <- as.vector(ext(x)) / 1000
  crs(x) <- km
  x
}

frame_at_scale <- function(x, scale, width_in, height_in, crs = "EPSG:32605") {
  bb <- sf::st_bbox(sf::st_transform(x, crs))
  cx <- mean(bb[c("xmin", "xmax")]); cy <- mean(bb[c("ymin", "ymax")])
  hw <- width_in  * 0.0254 * scale / 2
  hh <- height_in * 0.0254 * scale / 2
  sf::st_bbox(c(xmin = cx - hw, ymin = cy - hh, xmax = cx + hw, ymax = cy + hh),
              crs = sf::st_crs(crs))
}

scale_label <- function(scale) paste0("1:", format(scale, big.mark = " ", scientific = F))

map_frame <- function(title, legend=tmap::tm_pos_out("right","center"), ...) {

  	frame = T, inner.margins = 0,

    legend.position = legend, legend.text.size = 0.55,
    legend.title.size = 0.65, component.autoscale = F)
}
```

# Abstract

```{r}
#| label: abstract-numbers
#| echo: true
#| output: false
struct_a <- as.matrix(read.csv("03.outputs/landscape_structure.csv", row.names = 1)); strip_a <- read.csv("03.outputs/statewide_strip.csv")  # the abstract renders before the chunks that compute its numbers, so it reads the copies they saved
regions_a <- as.matrix(read.csv("03.outputs/statewide_regions.csv", row.names = 1)); area_a <- read.csv("03.outputs/statewide_area.csv")
```

Outbreaks of the spruce beetle (*Dendroctonus rufipennis* (Kirby)) in Alaska have killed the largest spruce first, so the tallest stands are most at risk in the next outbreak. Managers rate that hazard from tree diameter, basal area, and spruce share measured on the ground, which no cruise covers statewide, and no study had tested whether radar measures of stand structure pick out the stands an outbreak kills. This study scored Sentinel-1 radar backscatter of 2014 to 2016, before the current outbreak reached the Susitna valley, and a canopy height map against a crown-scale map of the spruce killed there by 2021 (`r format(strip_a$n, big.mark = " ")` cells of 90 m), then pooled every scene over Alaska into a 90 m map of pre-outbreak backscatter tested against the aerial detection survey. The killed stands had returned more backscatter before the outbreak and were taller, `r sprintf("%.1f", struct_a["dead", "height_eth"])` m against `r sprintf("%.1f", struct_a["alive", "height_eth"])` m. At the threshold that best separated the two, the backscatter map classed `r sprintf("%.0f", 100 * strip_a$sens_VV)` per cent of the killed and `r sprintf("%.0f", 100 * strip_a$spec_VV)` per cent of the spared stands correctly, an overall accuracy of `r if (is.null(strip_a$acc_VV)) "NA" else sprintf("%.0f", 100 * strip_a$acc_VV)` per cent. On the Kenai Peninsula and in the Matanuska-Susitna Borough it marked `r sprintf("%.0f", 100 * regions_a["above_dead", "kenai"])` and `r sprintf("%.0f", 100 * regions_a["above_dead", "matsu"])` per cent of the attacked forest as susceptible and `r sprintf("%.0f", 100 * regions_a["above_living", "kenai"])` and `r sprintf("%.0f", 100 * regions_a["above_living", "matsu"])` per cent of the unattacked, respectively. In the Copper River basin, where attacked stands were `r sprintf("%.1f", regions_a["height_dead", "copper"])` m tall against `r sprintf("%.1f", regions_a["height_living", "copper"])` m, it marked `r if (max(regions_a[c("above_dead", "above_living"), "copper"]) < 0.01) "less than 1" else sprintf("%.0f", 100 * max(regions_a[c("above_dead", "above_living"), "copper"]))` per cent of either and only canopy height separated them. Backscatter and canopy height therefore marked the stands the beetle killed with no beetle data and no cruise in the spruce forest of Southcentral Alaska, but not in its open woodland. Of Alaska's `r format(round(area_a$forest_km2[area_a$region == "alaska"]), big.mark = " ")` km² of forest, `r sprintf("%.0f", 100 * area_a$susceptible_km2[area_a$region == "alaska"] / area_a$forest_km2[area_a$region == "alaska"])` per cent lay at or above the threshold, so the map shows managers which stands to protect first.

# Introduction

The spruce beetle, *Dendroctonus rufipennis* (Kirby) \[Coleoptera: Curculionidae: Scolytinae\], is a bark beetle whose hosts are all the spruces of North America, 'with preference for large-diameter, mature trees' [@Fettig_2026, p. 1]. Its brood takes one year or two to mature and summer warmth decides which, in that the larvae develop to adults within the first season when the bark is warm enough and otherwise pass the winter as larvae and emerge a year later [@Hansen_2001b]. In Utah, Colorado, and on the Kenai Peninsula, the best predictor of a one-year brood was the number of hours above 17 °C in the 40 to 90 days after the adults flew [@Hansen_2001], and a one-year cycle doubles the rate at which a population grows and spreads [@Raffa_2008, p. 511]. Between outbreaks the beetle breeds in windthrown and felled spruce, which it prefers to standing trees [@Schmid_1977, p. 11], and 'Once the availability of windthrown spruce is exhausted, mature adult spruce beetles often transition to attacking live spruces, which can lead to outbreaks' [@Fettig_2026, p. 1]. A living spruce defends itself with resin, and its 'defenses are overcome only when a critical minimum number of beetles are recruited to the host tree' [@Bentz_2010, p. 603], so a small population takes only weakened trees, although 'Larger or thick-phloemed trees provide greater resources for larval feeding, and yield higher rates of beetle replacement' [@Raffa_2008, p. 512]. @Raffa_2008 [p. 501] therefore described bark beetle outbreaks as eruptions that 'occur when key thresholds are surpassed, prior constraints cease to exert influence, and positive feedbacks amplify across scales'. The large spruce is therefore the host the beetle gains most from and the one it reaches only in numbers, so it is taken first when an outbreak begins and the average size of the trees attacked falls as the outbreak runs [@Massey_1954; @Schmid_1976].

In Alaska, the beetle's preferred hosts are Lutz spruce (*Picea × lutzii* Little) and white spruce (*P. glauca* (Moench) Voss) [@Fettig_2026], and its outbreaks have been more frequent and severe in Lutz spruce than in white or Sitka spruce (*P. sitchensis* (Bong.) Carrière) [@Holsten_1990]. They have recurred for as long as the record reaches. On the Kenai Peninsula, tree rings recorded regional outbreaks 'during the 1810s, 1850s, 1870–1880s, 1910s, and 1970–1980s', 'at a mean return interval of 52 years' [@Berg_2006, p. 219], and tree rings of 1601 to 2007 across south central and southwest Alaska gave 'evidence of regional-scale outbreaks dating from the mid-1700s', with the outbreaks since the 1990s, though within that range, showing 'greater spatiotemporal synchrony' than at any time in about 250 years [@Sherriff_2011, p. 1459]. On the Kenai Peninsula, the beetle killed 29 per cent of the white spruce of the Resurrection Creek watershed between 1976 and 1980, taking the larger diameter classes first and smaller trees as the unattacked ran out [@Werner_1983], and across Alaska it likewise killed the larger spruce [@Baker_1974; @Holsten_1984], in the Copper River basin the more so the larger and the slower growing the tree [@Doak_2004]. On the same peninsula, the attacked trees had grown more slowly than the unattacked and a large diameter predicted attack or death only when coupled with slow growth [@Hard_1983; @Hard_1985], and the Forest Service guide to those stands described the susceptible trees as 'often dominants or codominants in well-stocked stands' [@Hard_1985b, p. 7], so the trees the beetle takes first are often the tallest of the stand.

Weather set their timing. On the Kenai Peninsula, the outbreaks of 1971 to 1996 'were positively associated with the 5-year backwards running average of summer temperature', and @Berg_2006 [p. 219] suggested that warm temperature acted 'through a combination of increased overwinter survival, a doubling of the maturation rate from 2 years to 1 year, and regional drought-induced stress of mature host trees'. Across south central and southwest Alaska, 'El Niño years, combined with severe late-summer drought, appeared to contribute significantly to spruce beetle outbreaks', which the cool phase of the Pacific Decadal Oscillation, a pattern of Pacific Ocean temperatures that shifts every few decades, tended to precede [@Sherriff_2011, p. 1459]. In Utah and Colorado, outbreak years followed Decembers and preceding Septembers about 2 °C warmer than other years and five years of below normal precipitation [@Hebertson_2008, pp. 285-287], and in northwestern Colorado outbreaks were 'predicted best by interannual to multidecadal variability in drought, not by temperature alone' [@Hart_2014, p. 930]. The warmth works only where there are large trees to take, in that the Kenai relationship 'decoupled after 1996, presumably because spruce beetles had killed most of the susceptible mature spruce in the region' [@Berg_2006, p. 219]. From 1920 to 1989 about 847 000 ha of Alaska's spruce forest were infested, and the outbreak of 1990 to 2000 alone infested 1.19 million ha, 'approximately 40% more forest area than was infested the previous 70 years', which @Werner_2006 [p. 195] related 'to the relatively high densities of large-diameter spruce in an aging forest across the region and to a warming trend'. It peaked in 1996, when more than 500 000 ha of spruce stands were infested [@Holsten_2001]. The present outbreak has affected about 2 million acres of Southcentral Alaska, some 800 000 ha, since 2016, and had spread north to Cantwell and the Alaska Range by 2020 [@Zwieback_2024].

Hazard ratings, scores of how likely a stand is to be attacked, applied that preference to the stand. The first was Research Note RM-309 of the Rocky Mountain Forest and Range Experiment Station, in which @Schmid_1976 [p. 1] rated Engelmann spruce (*Picea engelmannii* Parry ex Engelm.) stands 'on the basis of physiographic location, tree diameter, basal area, and percentage of spruce in the canopy', the basal area being the cross-sectional area of the stems per hectare, and set the high class at well-drained creek bottoms, an average diameter above 41 cm among the spruce over 25 cm, a basal area above 34 m² per hectare and more than 65 per cent spruce in the canopy. Its diameter classes were drawn from the White River outbreak of the 1940s in Colorado, in which the average diameter of the infested trees 'decreased from 21 to 17 to 15' inches as the large trees were used up [@Schmid_1976, p. 2]. On the Kenai Peninsula, a decision tree on basal area, spruce share, the share of the spruce basal area in trees over 25 cm in diameter, elevation, and aspect predicted high hazard correctly for at least 73 per cent of the stands [@Reynolds_1994b]. The current Forest Service leaflet rates as most susceptible the stands in drainage bottoms whose spruce average more than 40 cm in diameter, whose basal area exceeds 34 m² per hectare and in which more than 60 per cent of the stand is live spruce [@Fettig_2026]. A rating also falls as an outbreak proceeds, so a stand is rated before the beetle arrives. In central Utah, stands rated high to mostly medium hazard before the outbreak of 1986 to 1998 were rated medium to primarily low by 1998, after average spruce diameter, basal area, and overstory spruce had fallen [@Dymerski_2001]. Every rating takes its diameter, basal area, and spruce share from a cruise, a ground inventory of the stand. The prevention a rating directs, thinning and partial cutting [@Hard_1985b; @Fettig_2007; @Hansen_2010; @Temperli_2014], therefore needs the susceptible stands found first.

Remote sensing of the outbreak has mapped the damage after it appeared rather than the stands at risk. Landsat composites and dense time series mapped spruce beetle mortality in Colorado and its subtle change [@Woodward_2018; @Ye_2021], and the sensitivity of a Landsat series to mortality depended on its severity [@Rodman_2021]. In the Susitna valley, about 90 per cent of the dead spruce mapped at crown scale on WorldView-2 imagery of 2021 stood in stands where dead crowns covered no more than 5 per cent of the ground [@Zwieback_2024, p. 412], and Landsat reflectance change related clearly to that cover only above 10 per cent [@Zwieback_2024]. Radar was scarcely used for insect damage before Sentinel-1 [@Hollaus_2019], and in Bavaria it has since been fitted to the vitality of spruce attacked by bark beetles [@Hechtl_2025].



Radar backscatter and canopy height measure the structure of a stand. Backscatter, the part of the radar pulse that a stand reflects back to the satellite, rises with the dry mass of the trees until it saturates, at about 100 tons per hectare at L-band [@Dobson_1992], and Sentinel-1 operates at the shorter C-band, where 'the C-band backscattering coefficient shows much less sensitivity to total above-ground biomass' [@Dobson_1992, p. 412]. Canopy height is now mapped worldwide at 10 m [@Lang_2023]. A map of tall stands is therefore a map of the large dominant spruce that the hazard ratings describe, drawn without a cruise.



No study had scored radar backscatter or a canopy height map against the stands a spruce beetle outbreak killed, or mapped the stands susceptible to the beetle across a region. This study tested two hypotheses derived from that literature, and @tbl-attributes lists the measures entered, the attribute of the hazard ratings each stands for and the direction expected in killed stands. The first was that the Sentinel-1 backscatter of a stand before an outbreak and its canopy height would rank the stands the outbreak killed above those it spared, because both measure the large dominant spruce the beetle takes first, tested in the Susitna valley against the crown-scale map of dead spruce that @Zwieback_2024 made from a WorldView-2 image of 2 August 2021. The second was that a statewide map of pre-outbreak backscatter would rank attacked above unattacked forest wherever the aerial detection survey, the yearly flights in which observers map forest damage from an aircraft, had recorded the outbreak, and where that test failed the map was to be narrowed to the regions in which it succeeded.

# Materials and methods

## Study area

```{r}
#| label: areas
#| echo: true
#| output: false
# Zwieback et al. (2024) dead spruce crown labels, Zenodo https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.10569990, CC-BY 4.0.
# The list files name the WorldView-2 image each area was delineated on.
lab_dir <- "02.inputs/zwieback-labels"
areas <- rbind(transform(read.csv(file.path(lab_dir, "gpkg/list"), colClasses = "character"), set = "training", dir = "gpkg"),
               transform(read.csv(file.path(lab_dir, "gpkg_validation/list_validation"), colClasses = "character"), set = "test", dir = "gpkg_validation"))
areas$year <- ifelse(areas$image == "014782712010_01", 2021L, 2013L)  # the post-outbreak image of 2021-08-02 and the pre-outbreak image of 2013-07-14
read_area <- function(i) lapply(c(extent = "_extent.gpkg", crowns = "_labels.gpkg"), function(s) sf::st_read(file.path(lab_dir, areas$dir[i], paste0(areas$roi[i], s)), quiet = TRUE))
info <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(areas)), read_area)
areas <- sf::st_sf(areas, crowns = sapply(info, function(a) nrow(a$crowns)), geometry = do.call(c, lapply(info, function(a) sf::st_geometry(a$extent))))
cells_csv <- "02.inputs/derived/tile_cells.csv"
if (!file.exists(cells_csv)) write.csv(do.call(rbind, lapply(which(areas$year == 2021), function(i) {  # dead crown cover of each 10 m cell, on the UTM 5N grid
  a <- info[[i]]; b <- sf::st_bbox(a$extent)
  tpl <- terra::rast(xmin = floor(b$xmin / 10) * 10, xmax = ceiling(b$xmax / 10) * 10, ymin = floor(b$ymin / 10) * 10, ymax = ceiling(b$ymax / 10) * 10, resolution = 10, crs = "EPSG:32605")
  f <- if (nrow(a$crowns)) terra::rasterize(terra::vect(a$crowns), tpl, cover = TRUE) else terra::init(tpl, 0); f[is.na(f)] <- 0
  d <- setNames(as.data.frame(f, xy = TRUE), c("x", "y", "dead"))
  data.frame(roi = areas$roi[i], set = areas$set[i], d[sf::st_intersects(sf::st_as_sf(d, coords = c("x", "y"), crs = 32605), a$extent, sparse = FALSE)[, 1], ])
})), cells_csv, row.names = FALSE)
cells <- read.csv(cells_csv, colClasses = c(roi = "character"))
used <- areas[areas$year == 2021, ]
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-study
#| echo: true
#| fig-cap: "The study area. Main map, Alaska in the Alaska Albers projection (EPSG:3338) over a shaded relief, with the spruce beetle damage mapped by the aerial detection survey from 2016 to 2024 in red, the four regions in which the statewide map was tested outlined in black, the validation strip of the Susitna valley in which Zwieback et al. (2024) mapped dead spruce crowns on a WorldView-2 image of 2 August 2021 framed in blue, and the two detail panels boxed. A, Cook Inlet, the Kenai Peninsula and the Susitna valley. B, the Copper River basin. The inset places Alaska in North America."
#| fig-width: 7.5
#| fig-height: 8
# USFS Forest Health Protection aerial detection survey damage areas, Alaska Region 10, all years.
# https://www.fs.usda.gov/foresthealth/docs/IDS_Data_for_Download/AK_Region10_AllYears.gdb.zip
# United States Census Bureau cartographic boundary file of states, 2023, 1:20,000,000.
# https://www2.census.gov/geo/tiger/GENZ2023/shp/cb_2023_us_state_20m.zip
# US Census TIGER/Line 2018 county boundaries, Earth Engine TIGER/2018/Counties (row `TIGER/2018/Counties` of 02.inputs/README.md).
# https://developers.google.com/earth-engine/datasets/catalog/TIGER_2018_Counties
# Natural Earth 1:10m rivers (layer rivers) and the US Census Bureau TIGER/Line places of Alaska (layer places_census, NAD83), held in 02.inputs/context/naturalearth.gpkg (row `naturalearth.gpkg` of 02.inputs/README.md).
# https://www.naturalearthdata.com/downloads/10m-physical-vectors/ and https://www.census.gov/geographies/mapping-files/time-series/geo/tiger-line-file.html
# Natural Earth 1:50m countries through the rnaturalearth package.
# https://www.naturalearthdata.com/downloads/50m-cultural-vectors/
# Terrain Tiles (Mapzen elevation, AWS Open Data) through the elevatr package, cached as 02.inputs/context/alaska_dem_z6.tif and insets_dem_z7.tif (row `terrain-tiles` of 02.inputs/README.md).
# https://registry.opendata.aws/terrain-tiles/
ads_ak <- sf::st_transform(sf::st_read("02.inputs/ids-region10/AK_Region10_AllYears.gdb", quiet = TRUE,
                   query = "SELECT SURVEY_YEAR, Shape FROM DAMAGE_AREAS_FLAT_AllYears_AK_Rgn10 WHERE DCA_CODE = 11009 AND SURVEY_YEAR BETWEEN 2016 AND 2024"), 3338)
frame <- sf::st_as_sfc(sf::st_bbox(sf::st_buffer(sf::st_convex_hull(sf::st_union(sf::st_transform(used, 3338))), 20000)))  # the label areas and 20 km around them
ads <- sf::st_intersection(ads_ak, frame)
states_zip <- "02.inputs/context/cb_2023_us_state_20m.zip"
if (!file.exists(states_zip)) download.file("https://www2.census.gov/geo/tiger/GENZ2023/shp/cb_2023_us_state_20m.zip", states_zip, mode = "wb")
alaska <- sf::st_transform(subset(sf::st_read(file.path("/vsizip", states_zip, "cb_2023_us_state_20m.shp"), quiet = TRUE), STUSPS == "AK"), 3338)
regions <- list(kenai = "02122", matsu = "02170", copper = "02261", interior = c("02068", "02090", "02240"))  # the Kenai Peninsula Borough, the Matanuska-Susitna Borough, the Valdez-Cordova census area holding the Copper River basin, and the Denali Borough, Fairbanks North Star Borough and Southeast Fairbanks census area
region_names <- c(kenai = "Kenai Peninsula", matsu = "Matanuska-Susitna", copper = "Copper River", interior = "Interior")
regions_geojson <- "02.inputs/context/regions_tiger2018.geojson"
if (!file.exists(regions_geojson)) download.file(ee$FeatureCollection("TIGER/2018/Counties")$filter(ee$Filter$inList("GEOID", as.list(unname(unlist(regions)))))$getDownloadURL("geojson"), regions_geojson, quiet = TRUE)  # unnamed, or reticulate sends a dictionary
cty <- sf::st_transform(sf::st_read(regions_geojson, quiet = TRUE), 3338)
reg_sf <- sf::st_cast(do.call(rbind, lapply(names(regions), function(nm) sf::st_sf(region = nm, geometry = sf::st_union(sf::st_geometry(cty[cty$GEOID %in% regions[[nm]], ]))))), "MULTIPOLYGON")  # one multipolygon per region, so that terra transfers every part
reg_sf$name <- region_names[reg_sf$region]
ne_gpkg <- "02.inputs/context/naturalearth.gpkg"
rivers <- sf::st_transform(sf::st_read(ne_gpkg, layer = "rivers", quiet = TRUE), 3338)
towns <- sf::st_transform(sf::st_read(ne_gpkg, layer = "places_census", quiet = TRUE)[, "name"], 3338)  # the Alaska census places; the world layer holds namesakes such as the Valdez of Ecuador
towns <- towns[towns$name %in% c("Anchorage", "Fairbanks", "Juneau", "Kenai", "Homer", "Seward", "Valdez", "Palmer", "Talkeetna", "Glennallen", "Copper Center", "Chitina", "Nome", "Bethel"), ]
towns <- towns[!duplicated(towns$name), ]; sf::st_geometry(towns) <- "geometry"; sf::st_geometry(rivers) <- "geometry"  # the GeoPackage names the column geom
box_ll <- sf::st_as_sfc(sf::st_bbox(c(xmin = -180, ymin = 48, xmax = -125, ymax = 74), crs = 4326))
countries <- sf::st_transform(sf::st_make_valid(sf::st_crop(sf::st_make_valid(rnaturalearth::ne_countries(scale = "medium", country = c("Canada", "Russia"), returnclass = "sf")), box_ll)), 3338)  # the land beside Alaska, cropped before the projection so that the antimeridian does not fold it
dem_tif <- "02.inputs/context/alaska_dem_z6.tif"
if (!file.exists(dem_tif)) terra::writeRaster(terra::rast(elevatr::get_elev_raster(alaska, z = 6, clip = "locations")), dem_tif)  # about 2.4 km cells over the state
hill <- function(d, z = 3) { s <- terra::terrain(d * z, c("slope", "aspect"), unit = "radians");  # the elevation is exaggerated z times so that relief shows at these cell sizes
  h <- terra::shade(s$slope, s$aspect, angle = 45, direction = 315); terra::crs(h) <- "EPSG:3338"; h }  # the tiles come back in the Albers grid of the polygon they were clipped to, without its code
hs_state <- hill(terra::rast(dem_tif), 8)
pad_box <- function(x, pad, pad_x = 0) { b <- sf::st_bbox(sf::st_buffer(sf::st_as_sfc(sf::st_bbox(x)), pad)); b["xmin"] <- b["xmin"] - pad_x; b["xmax"] <- b["xmax"] + pad_x; sf::st_as_sfc(b) }  # the bounding box of x, grown by pad metres, and by pad_x more on each side
box_a <- pad_box(rbind(towns[towns$name %in% c("Anchorage", "Kenai", "Homer", "Seward", "Palmer", "Talkeetna"), "name"], sf::st_sf(name = "strip", geometry = sf::st_transform(frame, 3338))), 40000, 90000)  # Cook Inlet, the Kenai Peninsula and the Susitna valley
box_b <- pad_box(towns[towns$name %in% c("Valdez", "Glennallen", "Copper Center", "Chitina"), ], 60000)  # the Copper River basin above Valdez
same_shape <- function(b, ratio) { bb <- sf::st_bbox(b); w <- unname(bb["xmax"] - bb["xmin"]); h <- unname(bb["ymax"] - bb["ymin"])  # grow the shorter side so that the box is ratio times wider than tall, so the two panels share one height
  if (w / h < ratio) { d <- (h * ratio - w) / 2; bb["xmin"] <- bb["xmin"] - d; bb["xmax"] <- bb["xmax"] + d } else { d <- (w / ratio - h) / 2; bb["ymin"] <- bb["ymin"] - d; bb["ymax"] <- bb["ymax"] + d }
  sf::st_as_sfc(bb) }
box_a <- same_shape(box_a, 1.25); box_b <- same_shape(box_b, 1.25)
panel_letter <- function(b, lab) { bb <- sf::st_bbox(b); annotate("label", x = bb["xmin"] + 0.06 * (bb["xmax"] - bb["xmin"]), y = bb["ymax"] - 0.07 * (bb["ymax"] - bb["ymin"]), label = lab, size = 3.4, fontface = "bold", label.size = 0.2) }
ins_tif <- "02.inputs/context/insets_dem_z7.tif"
if (!file.exists(ins_tif)) terra::writeRaster(terra::rast(elevatr::get_elev_raster(sf::st_as_sf(sf::st_union(box_a, box_b)), z = 7, clip = "bbox")), ins_tif)  # about 1 km cells over the two detail panels
hs_ins <- terra::mask(hill(terra::rast(ins_tif)), terra::vect(alaska))
panel <- function(hs, xlim, ylim, tw, text_size = 2.3, river_lwd = 0.25, scale_hint = 0.25, scale_loc = "bl") ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = countries, fill = "#E6E2D8", colour = NA) + tidyterra::geom_spatraster(data = hs) + scale_fill_gradient(low = "grey45", high = "white", na.value = NA, guide = "none") +
  geom_sf(data = alaska, fill = "#EEDFB8", alpha = 0.5, colour = "grey35", linewidth = 0.2) + geom_sf(data = rivers, colour = "#3F7FBF", linewidth = river_lwd) +
  geom_sf(data = ads_ak, fill = "#C0392B", colour = "#C0392B", linewidth = 0.1) + geom_sf(data = reg_sf, fill = NA, colour = "black", linewidth = 0.4) + geom_sf(data = frame, fill = NA, colour = "#1F618D", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_sf(data = tw, colour = "black", fill = "#2ECC40", shape = 21, size = 1.6, stroke = 0.3) + ggrepel::geom_text_repel(data = tw, aes(label = name, geometry = geometry), stat = "sf_coordinates", size = text_size, fontface = "bold", seed = 2, min.segment.length = 0, box.padding = 0.25) +
  ggspatial::annotation_scale(location = scale_loc, width_hint = scale_hint, text_cex = 0.55, height = grid::unit(0.12, "cm"), plot_unit = "m", unit_category = "metric") +  # the plot unit is given because the bar cannot read it from a coord_sf without a datum
  coord_sf(xlim = xlim, ylim = ylim, expand = FALSE, datum = NA) + labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) + th + theme(panel.background = element_rect(fill = "#CFE3F3"), panel.border = element_rect(colour = "black", fill = NA, linewidth = 0.5), panel.grid.major = element_blank(), axis.text = element_blank(), axis.ticks = element_blank(), plot.margin = grid::unit(c(1, 1, 1, 1), "pt"))
main_towns <- towns[towns$name %in% c("Anchorage", "Fairbanks", "Juneau", "Nome", "Bethel"), ]
box_lab <- function(b, lab) annotate("label", x = sf::st_bbox(b)["xmax"] - 30000, y = sf::st_bbox(b)["ymax"] - 40000, label = lab, size = 2.8, fontface = "bold", label.size = 0.2, label.padding = grid::unit(0.1, "lines"))
main <- panel(hs_state, c(-1.55e6, 1.45e6), c(4.2e5, 2.35e6), main_towns, text_size = 2.5, river_lwd = 0.2, scale_hint = 0.2) +
  geom_sf(data = box_a, fill = NA, colour = "black", linewidth = 0.5) + geom_sf(data = box_b, fill = NA, colour = "black", linewidth = 0.5) + box_lab(box_a, "A") + box_lab(box_b, "B") +
  ggrepel::geom_label_repel(data = reg_sf, aes(label = name, geometry = geometry), stat = "sf_coordinates", size = 2.2, label.size = 0.2, seed = 1, min.segment.length = 0, nudge_x = c(-300000, -380000, 340000, 420000), nudge_y = c(-230000, 170000, -110000, 260000)) +  # kenai, matsu, copper, interior
  ggspatial::annotation_north_arrow(location = "tr", style = ggspatial::north_arrow_minimal(text_size = 7), height = grid::unit(0.9, "cm"), width = grid::unit(0.6, "cm")) +
  coord_sf(xlim = c(-1.55e6, 1.45e6), ylim = c(4.2e5, 2.35e6), expand = FALSE, datum = NA)  # set again last, because every geom_sf added after a coord_sf replaces it with a default one
world <- sf::st_transform(sf::st_make_valid(sf::st_crop(sf::st_make_valid(rnaturalearth::ne_countries(scale = "medium", returnclass = "sf")), sf::st_as_sfc(sf::st_bbox(c(xmin = -180, ymin = 30, xmax = -50, ymax = 85), crs = 4326)))), 3338)
locator <- ggplot() + geom_sf(data = world, fill = "#E6E2D8", colour = "grey60", linewidth = 0.15) + geom_sf(data = alaska, fill = "#C0392B", colour = NA) +
  annotate("text", x = c(-2.3e6, 2.2e6, 0.1e6, 0.6e6, -0.4e6), y = c(2.2e6, 0.9e6, 3.0e6, -1.3e6, 1.6e6), label = c("Russia", "Canada", "Arctic Ocean", "Pacific Ocean", "Alaska"), size = c(1.8, 1.8, 1.8, 1.8, 2), fontface = c("plain", "plain", "italic", "italic", "bold")) +
  coord_sf(xlim = c(-3.2e6, 3.4e6), ylim = c(-1.9e6, 3.5e6), expand = FALSE, datum = NA) + theme_void() + theme(panel.background = element_rect(fill = "#CFE3F3", colour = "black", linewidth = 0.4))
pan_a <- panel(hs_ins, sf::st_bbox(box_a)[c("xmin", "xmax")], sf::st_bbox(box_a)[c("ymin", "ymax")], towns[towns$name %in% c("Anchorage", "Kenai", "Homer", "Seward", "Palmer", "Talkeetna"), ], scale_hint = 0.35, scale_loc = "br") + panel_letter(box_a, "A")
pan_b <- panel(hs_ins, sf::st_bbox(box_b)[c("xmin", "xmax")], sf::st_bbox(box_b)[c("ymin", "ymax")], towns[towns$name %in% c("Valdez", "Glennallen", "Copper Center", "Chitina"), ], scale_hint = 0.35) + panel_letter(box_b, "B")
(main + patchwork::inset_element(locator, left = 0.58, bottom = 0.04, right = 0.84, top = 0.34)) / (pan_a | pan_b) + patchwork::plot_layout(heights = c(1 / 1.554, 0.5 / 1.25))  # the main map is 1.554 times wider than tall and each detail panel 1.25, so the rows fill the width without gutters
```

Alt text: Three maps. The main map shows Alaska over shaded relief with the spruce beetle damage of the 2016 to 2024 aerial detection survey in red, the four test regions outlined in black and labelled, the Susitna valley validation strip framed in blue, major rivers in blue, the towns of Anchorage, Fairbanks, Juneau, Nome and Bethel, two boxes marked A and B, a scale bar, a north arrow and an inset locating Alaska between Russia and Canada. Panel A enlarges Cook Inlet, the Kenai Peninsula and the Susitna valley with the towns of Anchorage, Kenai, Homer, Seward, Palmer and Talkeetna. Panel B enlarges the Copper River basin with Glennallen and Valdez.

The study covered the forest of Alaska, `r format(round(area_a$forest_km2[area_a$region == "alaska"]), big.mark = " ")` km² of 10 m cells with a canopy height of 5 m or more, which Sentinel-1 imaged from October 2014 (@fig-study). White and black spruce (*P. mariana* (Mill.) Britton et al.), Alaska birch (*Betula neoalaskana* Sarg.) and trembling aspen (*Populus tremuloides* Michx.) form the forest of the Interior and the Southcentral lowlands, with Lutz spruce on the Kenai Peninsula and Sitka spruce along the coast. The validation strip lay along the Parks Highway in the Susitna valley, between `r sprintf("%.1f", sf::st_bbox(sf::st_transform(used, 4326))["ymin"])`° N and `r sprintf("%.1f", sf::st_bbox(sf::st_transform(used, 4326))["ymax"])`° N, where @Zwieback_2024 delineated dead spruce crowns. Within 20 km of the strip, the aerial detection survey mapped the most spruce beetle damage in `r names(which.max(tapply(as.numeric(sf::st_area(ads)), ads$SURVEY_YEAR, sum)))`, `r format(round(max(tapply(as.numeric(sf::st_area(ads)), ads$SURVEY_YEAR, sum)) / 1e4), big.mark = " ")` ha. The map was tested in four regions, the Kenai Peninsula Borough, which held most of the Alaska plot studies [@Werner_1983; @Hard_1983; @Reynolds_1994b], the Matanuska-Susitna Borough, which contains the strip, the Valdez-Cordova census area, which contains the Copper River basin of @Doak_2004, and the Denali, Fairbanks North Star, and Southeast Fairbanks areas of the Interior, which the outbreak had reached at Cantwell by 2020 [@Zwieback_2024].

## Reference data

The reference data were the dead spruce crowns that @Zwieback_2024 delineated by hand on a WorldView-2 image of 2 August 2021, `r sum(used$set == "training")` training areas of 512 m with `r format(sum(used$crowns[used$set == "training"]), big.mark = " ")` crowns and `r sum(used$set == "test")` test areas of 90 m with `r format(sum(used$crowns[used$set == "test"]), big.mark = " ")`, and their severity map, the fraction of each 90 m cell covered by dead spruce, reported with a root mean square error of 0.02. The severity map has no declared licence and was used for validation only. The `r sum(areas$crowns[areas$year == 2013])` crowns of the areas they delineated on a pre-outbreak image of 14 July 2013 were set aside. The delineators were 'not able to directly identify a tree's species, whether it was alive or dead, or the mortality agent when assembling the test data' [@Zwieback_2024, p. 418], so a crown is a dead spruce in an area of outbreak rather than a confirmed beetle kill. It records that the spruce stood dead on that date and not the year it died. Each area was divided into 10 m cells on the WGS 84 UTM zone 5N grid of the labels, `r format(nrow(cells), big.mark = " ")` cells in all, and the fraction of each covered by dead crowns was computed. The aerial detection survey of the Forest Service gave the second label, its damage polygons recording survey year, host, and mortality class and its surveyed-area polygons recording the ground the observers flew over. The Forest Inventory and Analysis plot and tree tables for Alaska [@Bechtold_2005] gave the ground check.

## Satellite data

```{r}
#| label: s1-flatten
#| echo: true
#| output: false
# Sentinel-1 GRD, Earth Engine COPERNICUS/S1_GRD.
# https://developers.google.com/earth-engine/datasets/catalog/COPERNICUS_S1_GRD
# Copernicus GLO-30 DEM, Earth Engine COPERNICUS/DEM/GLO30_2024_1.
# https://developers.google.com/earth-engine/datasets/catalog/COPERNICUS_DEM_GLO30_2024_1
s1 <- ee$ImageCollection("COPERNICUS/S1_GRD")$filter(ee$Filter$eq("instrumentMode", "IW"))$
  filter(ee$Filter$listContains("transmitterReceiverPolarisation", "VH"))
dem <- ee$ImageCollection("COPERNICUS/DEM/GLO30_2024_1")$select("DEM")$mosaic()
rad <- pi / 180
flatten <- function(img, bands = c("VV", "VH"), smooth = TRUE) {  # volume-model slope correction of Vollrath et al. (2020), layover and shadow masked; smooth applies the 3 by 3 mean
  theta <- img$select("angle")$multiply(rad)
  phi <- ee$Image$constant(ee$Terrain$aspect(img$select("angle"))$reduceRegion(ee$Reducer$mean(), img$geometry(), 1000)$get("aspect"))$multiply(rad)
  a_r <- ee$Terrain$slope(dem)$multiply(rad)$tan()$multiply(phi$subtract(ee$Terrain$aspect(dem)$multiply(rad))$cos())$atan()
  g0 <- ee$Image$constant(10)$pow(img$select(bands)$divide(10))$divide(theta$cos())
  corr <- ee$Image$constant(pi / 2)$subtract(theta)$add(a_r)$tan()$divide(ee$Image$constant(pi / 2)$subtract(theta)$tan())
  g <- g0$divide(corr); if (smooth) g <- g$focalMean(1.5)
  ee$Image(g$log10()$multiply(10)$updateMask(a_r$lt(theta)$And(a_r$gt(theta$subtract(pi / 2))))$
    copyProperties(img, list("system:time_start", "relativeOrbitNumber_start")))
}
```

Sentinel-1 ground range detected scenes in interferometric wide swath mode were read in Google Earth Engine [@Gorelick_2017], where each had been corrected for thermal noise, calibrated, terrain corrected, and converted to decibels. Following the analysis-ready preparation of @Mullissa_2021, backscatter was normalized for slope with the volume scattering model of @Vollrath_2020, which also masks layover and radar shadow, on the Copernicus 30 m elevation model, because north of 60° N @Mullissa_2021 advised an alternative to the Shuttle Radar Topography Mission. Speckle was reduced with a 3 by 3 mean in linear power. The strip is imaged by the ascending orbit 65 and the descending orbit 131, which view the forest from opposite sides at different incidence angles, so the two were kept apart in the validation and pooled after a correction for incidence angle in the statewide map. Canopy height came from three sources. The ETH Zurich model of 2020 fitted the heights measured by the Global Ecosystem Dynamics Investigation lidar on the International Space Station to Sentinel-2 imagery at 10 m [@Lang_2023], and two surface models less the 10 m terrain model of the United States Geological Survey 3D Elevation Program gave the other two, the Copernicus GLO-30 surface from X-band radar of 2011 to 2015 and the ArcticDEM mosaic from optical stereo at 2 m [@Porter_2023]. The yearly mosaics of the Phased Array L-band Synthetic Aperture Radar (PALSAR) on the Advanced Land Observing Satellite (ALOS) of the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency gave L-band backscatter at 25 m in HH and HV, the horizontal pulse with its horizontal or vertical return [@Shimada_2014], and the LANDFIRE existing vegetation type gave the vegetation class of each cell [@Rollins_2009]. The conifer top cover of 2020 from the Arctic-Boreal Vulnerability Experiment [@Macander_2022] defined living forest.

## Literature review

```{r}
#| label: review-terms
#| echo: true
#| output: false
terms_csv <- "04.references/review/search-terms.csv"
if (!file.exists(terms_csv)) {  # every candidate term from the title and keywords, selected by hand in the file and frozen with the protocol
  front <- rmarkdown::yaml_front_matter("01.manuscript/manuscript.qmd")
  small <- c("a", "an", "and", "as", "at", "by", "do", "does", "for", "from", "how", "in", "into", "is", "its", "of", "on", "or", "the", "to", "under", "using", "versus", "what", "why", "with", "across")
  phrases <- function(x) x |> stringr::str_to_lower() |> stringr::str_remove_all("[*_]") |> stringr::str_replace_all("[^[:alnum:][:space:]-]", " | ") |>
    stringr::str_replace_all(paste0("\\b(", paste(small, collapse = "|"), ")\\b"), " | ") |> stringr::str_split_1("\\|") |> stringr::str_squish() |> purrr::keep(function(p) nchar(p) > 2)
  dir.create(dirname(terms_csv), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  dplyr::bind_rows(tibble::tibble(term = stringr::str_squish(stringr::str_to_lower(unlist(front$keywords))), source = "keywords"), tibble::tibble(term = phrases(front$title), source = "title")) |>
    dplyr::distinct(term, .keep_all = TRUE) |> dplyr::mutate(question = NA, concept = NA) |> readr::write_csv(terms_csv, na = "")
}
```

```{r}
#| label: review-queries
#| echo: true
#| output: false
front <- rmarkdown::yaml_front_matter("01.manuscript/manuscript.qmd")
declared <- stringr::str_to_lower(paste(front$title, paste(unlist(front$keywords), collapse = " ")))
term_regex <- function(x) if (stringr::str_ends(x, "\\*")) paste0("\\b", stringr::str_escape(stringr::str_remove(x, "\\*$"))) else paste0("\\b", stringr::str_escape(x), "\\b")
terms <- readr::read_csv(terms_csv, col_types = readr::cols(.default = "c")) |> dplyr::filter(!is.na(question), !is.na(concept)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(term = stringr::str_to_lower(term)) |> tidyr::separate_longer_delim(question, " ")
stray <- terms$term[!purrr::map_lgl(terms$term, function(x) stringr::str_detect(declared, term_regex(x)))]
if (nrow(terms) == 0) stop("No search terms selected in ", terms_csv)
if (length(stray) > 0) stop("Not in the title or keywords: ", paste(unique(stray), collapse = ", "))  # a new word enters the search only by entering the keywords first
queries <- terms |> dplyr::summarise(.by = c(question, concept), group = paste(term, collapse = "|")) |>
  dplyr::summarise(.by = question, route = paste(c(dplyr::first(question), concept), collapse = "-"), concepts = paste(group, collapse = " AND "))
```

```{r}
#| label: review-store
#| echo: true
#| output: false
store_csv <- "02.inputs/derived/review-store-hits.csv"; log_csv <- "02.inputs/derived/review-search-log.csv"
if (!file.exists(store_csv)) {
  # library-science manifest and source notes, the central store at Github/library-science, https://github.com/seamusrobertmurphy/library-science
  manifest <- readr::read_csv("../library-science/library/manifest.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
  notes <- tibble::tibble(path = list.files("../library-science/sources", "\\.md$", full.names = TRUE)) |>
    dplyr::mutate(key = tools::file_path_sans_ext(basename(path)), note = purrr::map_chr(path, function(p) paste(readLines(p, warn = FALSE), collapse = " ")))
  store <- manifest |> dplyr::filter(status %in% c("verified", "filed", "unverified"), !is.na(title) | !is.na(key)) |> dplyr::left_join(dplyr::select(notes, key, note), by = "key") |> dplyr::mutate(text = stringr::str_to_lower(paste(title, note)))
  term_pat <- function(x) if (stringr::str_ends(x, "\\*")) paste0(stringr::str_remove(x, "\\*$"), "\\w*") else paste0(x, "\\b")
  hits <- purrr::pmap(queries, function(question, route, concepts) {
    patterns <- purrr::map_chr(stringr::str_split_1(concepts, " AND "), function(g) paste0("\\b(", paste(purrr::map_chr(stringr::str_split_1(g, "\\|"), term_pat), collapse = "|"), ")"))
    keep <- purrr::reduce(purrr::map(patterns, function(r) stringr::str_detect(store$text, r)), `&`)
    store[keep, ] |> dplyr::transmute(question, route = paste0("store-", route), key, doi, title, year, venue = container, source_note = dplyr::if_else(has_source_note == "yes", key, NA)) }) |> purrr::list_rbind()
  readr::write_csv(hits, store_csv)
  queries |> dplyr::transmute(strand = "library-science", route = paste0("store-", route), query = concepts, date = as.character(Sys.Date())) |>
    dplyr::left_join(dplyr::count(hits, route, name = "retrieved"), by = "route") |> dplyr::mutate(retrieved = tidyr::replace_na(retrieved, 0L), reported_total = retrieved, cap = NA, capped = FALSE, error = NA) |> readr::write_csv(log_csv)
}
```

```{r}
#| label: review-semantic-scholar
#| echo: true
#| output: false
s2_csv <- "02.inputs/derived/review-s2-hits.csv"
if (!file.exists(s2_csv)) {
  search_s2 <- function(question, route, concepts, cap = 3000) {
    query <- paste(purrr::map_chr(stringr::str_split_1(concepts, " AND "), function(g) paste0("(", paste(purrr::map_chr(stringr::str_split_1(g, "\\|"), function(x) if (grepl(" ", x)) paste0('"', x, '"') else x), collapse = " | "), ")")), collapse = " + ")
    papers <- list(); token <- NULL; total <- NA
    repeat {
      # Semantic Scholar Academic Graph bulk search, https://api.semanticscholar.org/api-docs/graph#tag/Paper-Data/operation/get_graph_paper_bulk_search
      body <- httr2::request("https://api.semanticscholar.org/graph/v1/paper/search/bulk") |> httr2::req_url_query(query = query, fields = "title,year,venue,externalIds,citationCount,publicationTypes,abstract", token = token) |>
        httr2::req_retry(max_tries = 10, backoff = function(i) 5 * i) |> httr2::req_perform() |> httr2::resp_body_json()
      total <- body$total; token <- body$token; papers <- c(papers, body$data); Sys.sleep(1.5)
      if (is.null(token) || length(papers) >= cap) break }
    works <- purrr::list_rbind(purrr::map(papers, function(w) tibble::tibble(doi = w$externalIds$DOI %||% NA_character_, title = w$title %||% NA_character_, year = w$year %||% NA_integer_, venue = w$venue %||% NA_character_, type = paste(unlist(w$publicationTypes), collapse = " "), citations = w$citationCount %||% NA_integer_, abstract = w$abstract %||% NA_character_)))
    list(hits = dplyr::mutate(works, question, route = paste0("s2-", route), .before = 1), log = tibble::tibble(strand = "semantic-scholar", route = paste0("s2-", route), query, date = as.character(Sys.Date()), retrieved = nrow(works), reported_total = total, cap, capped = total > cap, error = NA)) }
  runs <- purrr::pmap(queries, search_s2)
  readr::write_csv(purrr::list_rbind(purrr::map(runs, "hits")), s2_csv)
  readr::read_csv(log_csv, col_types = readr::cols(.default = "c")) |> dplyr::bind_rows(purrr::list_rbind(purrr::map(runs, "log")) |> dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(dplyr::everything(), as.character))) |> readr::write_csv(log_csv)
}
```

```{r}
#| label: review-openalex
#| echo: true
#| output: false
oa_csv <- "02.inputs/derived/review-openalex-hits.csv"
if (!file.exists(oa_csv)) {
  stems <- c("susceptib*" = "susceptible OR susceptibility", "map*" = "map OR mapping OR mapped OR maps")  # OpenAlex takes no wildcard, so each stem is written out
  search_oa <- function(question, route, concepts, cap = 3000) {
    query <- paste(purrr::map_chr(stringr::str_split_1(concepts, " AND "), function(g) paste0("(", paste(purrr::map_chr(stringr::str_split_1(g, "\\|"), function(x) if (x %in% names(stems)) stems[[x]] else if (grepl(" ", x)) paste0('"', x, '"') else x), collapse = " OR "), ")")), collapse = " AND ")
    works <- list(); cursor <- "*"; total <- NA
    repeat {
      # OpenAlex works search, https://docs.openalex.org/api-entities/works/search-works
      body <- httr2::request("https://api.openalex.org/works") |> httr2::req_url_query(filter = paste0("title_and_abstract.search:", query), `per-page` = 200, cursor = cursor, mailto = "seamusrobertmurphy@gmail.com", select = "id,doi,title,publication_year,type,cited_by_count,primary_location,abstract_inverted_index") |>
        httr2::req_retry(max_tries = 8, backoff = function(i) 5 * i, is_transient = function(r) httr2::resp_status(r) %in% c(401, 429, 500, 503)) |> httr2::req_perform() |> httr2::resp_body_json()  # titles and abstracts, the same scope as the Semantic Scholar strand; a 401 from OpenAlex has been transient
      total <- body$meta$count; cursor <- body$meta$next_cursor; works <- c(works, body$results); Sys.sleep(0.5)
      if (is.null(cursor) || length(body$results) == 0 || length(works) >= cap) break }
    abstract <- function(ii) if (is.null(ii)) NA_character_ else { pos <- unlist(ii, use.names = FALSE); paste(rep(names(ii), lengths(ii))[order(pos)], collapse = " ") }  # the inverted index back into the abstract
    hits <- purrr::list_rbind(purrr::map(works, function(w) tibble::tibble(doi = if (is.null(w$doi)) NA_character_ else sub("^https://doi.org/", "", w$doi), title = w$title %||% NA_character_, year = w$publication_year %||% NA_integer_,
      venue = w$primary_location$source$display_name %||% NA_character_, type = w$type %||% NA_character_, citations = w$cited_by_count %||% NA_integer_, abstract = abstract(w$abstract_inverted_index))))
    list(hits = dplyr::mutate(hits, question, route = paste0("oa-", route), .before = 1), log = tibble::tibble(strand = "openalex", route = paste0("oa-", route), query, date = as.character(Sys.Date()), retrieved = nrow(hits), reported_total = total, cap, capped = total > cap, error = NA)) }
  runs <- purrr::pmap(queries, search_oa)
  readr::write_csv(purrr::list_rbind(purrr::map(runs, "hits")), oa_csv)
  readr::read_csv(log_csv, col_types = readr::cols(.default = "c")) |> dplyr::bind_rows(purrr::list_rbind(purrr::map(runs, "log")) |> dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(dplyr::everything(), as.character))) |> readr::write_csv(log_csv)
}
```

```{r}
#| label: review-chase
#| echo: true
#| output: false
central <- c("10.1139/x83-097", "10.1093/forestscience/31.4.839", "10.1139/x94-268", "10.1139/x83-014", "10.1016/j.isprsjprs.2024.05.013")  # Hard et al. 1983, Hard 1985, Reynolds and Holsten 1994, Werner and Holsten 1983, Zwieback et al. 2024
chase_csv <- "02.inputs/derived/review-chase-hits.csv"
if (length(central) > 0 && !file.exists(chase_csv)) {
  chase <- function(seed_doi, direction) {
    # Semantic Scholar Academic Graph references and citations, https://api.semanticscholar.org/api-docs/graph#tag/Paper-Data
    resp <- httr2::request(paste0("https://api.semanticscholar.org/graph/v1/paper/DOI:", seed_doi, "/", direction)) |> httr2::req_url_query(fields = "title,year,venue,externalIds,abstract", limit = 1000) |>
      httr2::req_retry(max_tries = 10, backoff = function(i) 5 * i) |> httr2::req_error(is_error = function(r) httr2::resp_status(r) == 429) |> httr2::req_perform(); Sys.sleep(1.5)
    if (httr2::resp_status(resp) != 200) return(tibble::tibble(seed = seed_doi, route = paste0("chase-", direction), error = httr2::resp_status_desc(resp)))
    key <- if (direction == "references") "citedPaper" else "citingPaper"
    purrr::list_rbind(purrr::map(httr2::resp_body_json(resp)$data, function(w) tibble::tibble(doi = w[[key]]$externalIds$DOI %||% NA_character_, title = w[[key]]$title %||% NA_character_, year = w[[key]]$year %||% NA_integer_, venue = w[[key]]$venue %||% NA_character_, abstract = w[[key]]$abstract %||% NA_character_))) |>
      dplyr::mutate(seed = seed_doi, route = paste0("chase-", direction), .before = 1) }
  readr::write_csv(purrr::list_rbind(purrr::pmap(tidyr::expand_grid(seed_doi = central, direction = c("references", "citations")), chase)), chase_csv)
}
```

```{r}
review_counts <- c(retrieved = sum(search_log$retrieved), unique = sum(!records$questions %in% c("chase", "hand")), chased = sum(records$questions == "chase"), hand = sum(records$questions == "hand"),  # the three strands, the citation chase and the records added by hand
  screened = nrow(records), included = sum(records$decision == "include", na.rm = TRUE), excluded = sum(records$decision == "exclude", na.rm = TRUE), full_text = sum(records$full_text == "yes", na.rm = TRUE), abstract_only = sum(records$decision == "include" & records$full_text == "abstract", na.rm = TRUE))
```

The literature behind the hypotheses was reviewed under a protocol frozen on 14 October 2026, with questions on the tree and stand attributes that predict attack, on the remote sensing of spruce beetle damage, and on whether a susceptibility map had been made before from radar or canopy height data without a field cruise. Queries built from the title and keywords were run that day in the author's reference store, the Semantic Scholar bulk search, and OpenAlex and returned `r format(review_counts["retrieved"], big.mark = " ")` records, `r review_counts["unique"]` of them unique, one round of backward and forward citation chasing from five central records added `r review_counts["chased"]`, and `r review_counts["hand"]` were added by hand. One reader screened all `r review_counts["screened"]` on title and abstract and retained `r review_counts["included"]`, every retained record behind an expected direction was read in full where its text could be reached, and the `r review_counts["abstract_only"]` whose text could not be reached are cited only for what their abstracts state.

## Stand validation

```{r}
#| label: s1-samples
#| echo: true
#| output: false
samp_dir <- "02.inputs/derived/tile_samples"
months <- seq(as.Date("2017-06-01"), as.Date("2021-08-01"), by = "month"); ym <- format(months, "%Y%m"); orbits <- c(65L, 131L)
composite <- function(col, bands, o, g, m) col$filterBounds(g)$filter(ee$Filter$eq("relativeOrbitNumber_start", o))$  # the median of the slope-corrected scenes of one orbit in one month
  filterDate(format(m), format(seq(m, by = "month", length.out = 2)[2]))$map(function(img) flatten(img, bands))$median()$rename(paste0(bands, o, "_", format(m, "%Y%m")))
sample_areas <- function(dir, comps) {  # sampled at the centre of every 10 m cell of every label area, one file per area
  dir.create(dir, showWarnings = FALSE)
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(used))) {
    out <- file.path(dir, paste0(used$roi[i], ".csv")); if (file.exists(out)) next
    xy <- sf::st_coordinates(sf::st_transform(used$geometry[i], 4326))
    g <- ee$Geometry$Polygon(list(lapply(seq_len(nrow(xy)), function(k) c(xy[k, 1], xy[k, 2]))))
    f <- tryCatch(ee$Image$cat(comps(g))$sample(region = g, scale = 10, projection = "EPSG:32605", geometries = TRUE, dropNulls = FALSE)$getInfo()$features,
                  error = function(e) if (grepl("concurren|Too Many Requests|timed out|memory", conditionMessage(e))) NULL else stop(e))
    if (is.null(f)) next  # left for the next pass when Earth Engine refuses the request under load
    p <- sf::st_coordinates(sf::st_transform(sf::st_as_sf(data.frame(t(sapply(f, function(z) unlist(z$geometry$coordinates)))), coords = 1:2, crs = 4326), 32605))
    write.csv(data.frame(roi = used$roi[i], x = round((p[, 1] - 5) / 10) * 10 + 5, y = round((p[, 2] - 5) / 10) * 10 + 5,
                         dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(f, function(z) Filter(Negate(is.null), z$properties)))), out, row.names = FALSE)
  }
}
spec <- expand.grid(o = orbits, m = format(months), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
sample_areas(samp_dir, function(g) unname(Map(function(o, m) composite(s1, c("VV", "VH"), o, g, as.Date(m)), spec$o, spec$m)))
```

The first hypothesis was tested on the stands of the label areas and then on the landscape. For every month from October 2014 to August 2021, the month of the label image, the median slope-corrected backscatter of each orbit was composited in Earth Engine and sampled at the centre of every 10 m cell of every label area. From June 2017, backscatter in VV and VH, the polarizations that send a vertical pulse and receive its vertical or horizontal return, was available on both orbits, and before then VV on both orbits with VH on the ascending orbit in scattered months from April 2015.

```{r}
#| label: series
#| echo: true
#| output: false
bands <- paste0(c("VV", "VH"), rep(orbits, each = 2))
samples <- merge(cells, dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(list.files(samp_dir, "\\.csv$", full.names = TRUE), read.csv, colClasses = c(roi = "character"))), by = c("roi", "x", "y"))
months_seen <- sapply(orbits, function(o) length(grep(paste0("^VV", o, "_"), names(samples))))
cube <- array(NA_real_, c(nrow(samples), length(ym), length(bands)), list(NULL, ym, bands))
for (b in bands) { has <- intersect(paste0(b, "_", ym), names(samples)); cube[, sub(".*_", "", has), b] <- as.matrix(samples[, has]) }
samples <- cbind(samples[, c("roi", "set", "x", "y", "dead")], setNames(as.data.frame(sf::st_coordinates(sf::st_transform(sf::st_as_sf(samples[, c("x", "y")], coords = c("x", "y"), crs = 32605), 4326))), c("lon", "lat")))
gaps <- mean(is.na(cube))
fill <- function(v) if (sum(!is.na(v)) < 2) v else approx(seq_along(v), v, seq_along(v), rule = 2)$y  # linear interpolation across months without a scene
cube <- aperm(apply(cube, c(1, 3), fill), c(2, 1, 3))
complete <- rowSums(is.na(cube)) == 0
window <- 24L; intervals <- c(1L, 2L, 3L, 6L)
series <- function(end, k = 1L, rows = seq_len(nrow(samples))) {  # the 24 months ending in `end`, averaged over blocks of k months
  j <- (match(end, ym) - window + 1):match(end, ym); blocks <- rep(seq_len(window / k), each = k); x <- cube[rows, j, , drop = FALSE]
  if (k > 1) x <- aperm(apply(x, c(1, 3), function(v) tapply(v, blocks, mean)), c(2, 1, 3))
  list(x = x, dates = months[j][!duplicated(blocks)])
}
as_sits <- function(rows, s) {  # a sits sample table, one time series per cell
  tb <- tibble::tibble(longitude = samples$lon[rows], latitude = samples$lat[rows], start_date = s$dates[1], end_date = tail(s$dates, 1),
                       label = ifelse(samples$dead[rows] >= 0.1, "dead", "alive"), cube = "S1",
                       time_series = lapply(seq_along(rows), function(i) tibble::as_tibble(cbind(data.frame(Index = s$dates), s$x[i, , ]))))
  class(tb) <- c("sits", class(tb)); tb
}
```

```{r}
ctr <- sf::st_as_sf(aggregate(cbind(x, y) ~ roi, samples[train, ], mean), coords = c("x", "y"), crs = 32605)
folds <- blockCV::cv_spatial(ctr, k = 5, size = 15000, selection = "random", seed = 20260915, progress = FALSE, report = FALSE, plot = FALSE)
```

```{r}
#| label: stands
#| echo: true
#| output: false
# ABoVE modelled top cover by plant functional type, conifer top cover 2020 (Macander and Nelson 2022), ORNL DAAC https://doi.org/10.3334/ORNLDAAC/2032, row `covariates/` of 02.inputs/README.md.
org <- aggregate(cbind(x0 = x, y0 = y) ~ roi, samples, min)
samples$stand <- paste(samples$roi, (samples$x - org$x0[match(samples$roi, org$roi)]) %/% 90, (samples$y - org$y0[match(samples$roi, org$roi)]) %/% 90)
g <- samples$stand %in% names(which(table(samples$stand) == 81))  # the 90 m cells wholly inside their area
stands <- aggregate(cbind(x, y, dead) ~ stand + roi + set, samples[g, ], mean); stands$fold <- samples$fold[match(stands$roi, samples$roi)]
ll <- sf::st_coordinates(sf::st_transform(sf::st_as_sf(stands, coords = c("x", "y"), crs = 32605), 4326)); stands$lon <- ll[, 1]; stands$lat <- ll[, 2]
sq <- sf::st_buffer(sf::st_as_sf(stands, coords = c("x", "y"), crs = 32605), 45, endCapStyle = "SQUARE")
conifer <- terra::rast("02.inputs/covariates/conifer_topcover_2020.tif"); sq <- terra::vect(sf::st_transform(sq, terra::crs(conifer)))
stands$conifer <- terra::extract(terra::crop(conifer, terra::ext(sq) + 100), sq, fun = mean, na.rm = TRUE, ID = FALSE)[, 1]
stands$label <- ifelse(stands$dead >= 0.01, "dead", ifelse(stands$dead == 0 & stands$conifer >= 5, "alive", NA))  # living forest is a stand with no dead crown and conifer top cover of 5 per cent or more
pre <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(list.files("02.inputs/derived/tile_samples_pre", "\\.csv$", full.names = TRUE), read.csv, colClasses = c(roi = "character")))
pre <- pre[match(paste(samples$roi, samples$x, samples$y), paste(pre$roi, pre$x, pre$y)), ]
ym_all <- format(seq(as.Date("2014-10-01"), as.Date("2021-08-01"), by = "month"), "%Y%m")
lin_mean <- function(M) { M <- as.matrix(M); 10 * log10(rowsum(10^(M / 10), samples$stand[g], na.rm = TRUE) / rowsum((!is.na(M)) + 0, samples$stand[g])) }  # the stand mean in linear power
scube <- array(NA_real_, c(nrow(stands), length(ym_all), length(bands)), list(stands$stand, ym_all, bands))
for (b in bands) { P <- pre[g, grep(paste0("^", b, "_"), names(pre)), drop = FALSE]; names(P) <- sub(".*_", "", names(P))
  M <- lin_mean(cbind(P, setNames(as.data.frame(cube[g, , b]), ym))); scube[, colnames(M), b] <- M[stands$stand, ] }
scube <- aperm(apply(scube, c(1, 3), fill), c(2, 1, 3))
```

```{r}
#| label: tempcnn-stands
#| echo: true
#| output: false
spred_csv <- "03.outputs/stand_predictions.csv"
designs <- list(VV_2014 = list(bands = c("VV65", "VV131"), from = "201410"), all_2017 = list(bands = bands, from = "201706"))
steps <- function(d) match(d$from, ym_all):length(ym_all)
ok_st <- function(d) rowSums(is.na(scube[, steps(d), d$bands, drop = FALSE])) == 0
as_sits_st <- function(rows, d) { j <- steps(d); dates <- as.Date(paste0(ym_all[j], "01"), "%Y%m%d")
  tb <- tibble::tibble(longitude = stands$lon[rows], latitude = stands$lat[rows], start_date = dates[1], end_date = tail(dates, 1), label = dplyr::coalesce(stands$label[rows], "alive"), cube = "S1",
                       time_series = lapply(rows, function(i) tibble::as_tibble(cbind(data.frame(Index = dates), scube[i, j, d$bands]))))
  class(tb) <- c("sits", class(tb)); tb }
fit_st <- function(rows, d) { set.seed(20260915); sits::sits_train(as_sits_st(rows, d), sits::sits_tempcnn(epochs = 60L, patience = 10L, seed = 20260915L, verbose = FALSE)) }
p_dead_st <- function(m, rows, d) sapply(sits::sits_classify(as_sits_st(rows, d), m, multicores = 1L, progress = FALSE)$predicted, function(z) z$dead)
strain_csv <- "03.outputs/stand_predictions_train.csv"  # each fold's network on its own training stands, for the overfitting ratio
if (!file.exists(spred_csv) || !file.exists(strain_csv)) { torch::torch_manual_seed(20260915); out <- list(); fits <- list()
  for (nm in names(designs)) { d <- designs[[nm]]; ok <- ok_st(d); lab <- ok & !is.na(stands$label); tr <- stands$set == "training"
    for (f in 1:5) { m <- fit_st(which(lab & tr & stands$fold != f), d); te <- which(ok & tr & stands$fold == f); fits[[paste(nm, f)]] <- m
      out[[length(out) + 1]] <- data.frame(stands[te, c("stand", "roi", "set", "fold", "dead", "conifer")], design = nm, p_dead = p_dead_st(m, te, d)) }
    m <- fit_st(which(lab & tr), d); te <- which(ok & !tr)
    out[[length(out) + 1]] <- data.frame(stands[te, c("stand", "roi", "set", "fold", "dead", "conifer")], design = nm, p_dead = p_dead_st(m, te, d)) }
  write.csv(do.call(rbind, out), spred_csv, row.names = FALSE)
  outt <- lapply(names(fits), function(k) { nm <- sub(" \\d$", "", k); f <- as.integer(sub("^.* ", "", k)); d <- designs[[nm]]; trn <- which(ok_st(d) & !is.na(stands$label) & stands$set == "training" & stands$fold != f)  # predicted after every fit, so the fits draw the same random numbers as before
    data.frame(stands[trn, c("stand", "roi", "set", "fold", "dead", "conifer")], design = nm, fold_model = f, p_dead = p_dead_st(fits[[k]], trn, d)) })
  write.csv(do.call(rbind, outt), strain_csv, row.names = FALSE) }
```

```{r}
#| label: accuracy-stands

auc <- function(x, y) { r <- rank(x); n1 <- sum(y); (sum(r[y]) - n1 * (n1 + 1) / 2) / (n1 * (length(y) - n1)) }  # the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, from the ranks
sp <- read.csv(spred_csv, colClasses = c(roi = "character")); sp$hit <- sp$p_dead >= 0.5
sp$label <- ifelse(sp$dead >= 0.01, TRUE, ifelse(sp$dead == 0 & sp$conifer >= 5, FALSE, NA))
score_st <- function(d) { d <- d[!is.na(d$label), ]; tp <- sum(d$hit & d$label)
  c(dead = sum(d$label), alive = sum(!d$label), precision = tp / sum(d$hit), recall = tp / sum(d$label), F1 = 2 * tp / (sum(d$hit) + sum(d$label)), AUC = auc(d$p_dead, d$label)) }
sacc <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(sp, list(sp$design, sp$set)), function(d) data.frame(design = d$design[1], set = d$set[1], t(score_st(d)))))
sp$bin <- ifelse(sp$dead == 0, ifelse(sp$conifer >= 5, "Living forest", "No conifer"), as.character(cut(sp$dead, c(0, 0.01, 0.02, 0.05, 0.1, 1), c("0 to 0.01", "0.01 to 0.02", "0.02 to 0.05", "0.05 to 0.1", "0.1 to 1"))))
sfloor <- with(sp[sp$set == "training", ], tapply(hit, list(bin, design), mean)); sfloor_n <- with(sp[sp$set == "training" & sp$design == "VV_2014", ], table(bin))
sbase <- sapply(designs, function(d) { r <- ok_st(d) & !is.na(stands$label) & stands$set == "training"; sapply(d$bands, function(b) auc(rowMeans(scube[r, steps(d), b]), stands$label[r] == "dead")) })  # one band averaged over the design's months, with no training
write.csv(sacc, "03.outputs/stand_accuracy.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r}
#| label: change-stands
#| echo: true
#| output: false
era <- function(a, b) which(ym_all >= a & ym_all <= b)
lab_st <- !is.na(stands$label) & stands$set == "training"; dead_st <- stands$label == "dead"
chg <- do.call(rbind, lapply(c("VV65", "VV131", "VH65"), function(b) data.frame(stand = stands$stand, band = b, dead = dead_st, labelled = lab_st, conifer = stands$conifer,  # VH on orbit 65 rests on the 11 dual-polarised months before June 2017, VH on orbit 131 has none
  pre = rowMeans(scube[, era("201410", "201612"), b]), late = rowMeans(scube[, era("201906", "202108"), b]))))  # each stand against its own level before the outbreak reached the area
chg$change <- chg$late - chg$pre
change <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(chg[chg$labelled, ], chg$band[chg$labelled]), function(d) data.frame(band = d$band[1],
  auc_pre = auc(d$pre, d$dead), auc_late = auc(d$late, d$dead), auc_change = auc(d$change, d$dead), auc_conifer = auc(d$conifer, d$dead),
  change_dead = mean(d$change[d$dead]), change_alive = mean(d$change[!d$dead]), t = unname(t.test(d$change[d$dead], d$change[!d$dead])$statistic), df = unname(t.test(d$change[d$dead], d$change[!d$dead])$parameter), p = t.test(d$change[d$dead], d$change[!d$dead])$p.value)))
write.csv(change, "03.outputs/stand_change.csv", row.names = FALSE)  # read by the abstract, which renders before this chunk
```

The test was made at the 90 m scale at which @Zwieback_2024 reported severity. Each 512 m label area was divided into 90 m cells, and the `r format(nrow(stands), big.mark = " ")` cells wholly inside their area took the mean dead crown fraction and the mean backscatter, in linear power, of their 81 cells of 10 m. A stand was dead at a dead crown fraction of 0.01 or more and living at 0 with conifer top cover of 5 per cent or more, so that the living class contained forest and not treeless ground. Because @Zwieback_2024 related the change in Landsat shortwave infrared reflectance to severity, the change in VV between October 2014 to December 2016, before the survey recorded damage in any label area, and June 2019 to August 2021 was scored beside the level of each period. Each was scored by the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, the chance that a killed stand drawn at random ranked above a living one, and the change was also tested with a Welch t-test, so that a difference that existed before the outbreak could be told from a change the outbreak made. To test whether the full monthly series added anything to the level, the temporal convolutional network of @Pelletier_2019, as implemented in sits [@Simoes_2021], was trained on the series of each stand. The `r nrow(ctr)` training areas were dealt to five spatial folds of 15 km hexagons by blockCV [@Valavi_2019], so that no stand was scored by a network that had seen its area.

## Landscape validation

```{r}
#| label: landscape
#| echo: true
#| output: false
# Zwieback (2023) spruce beetle outbreak severity, Southcentral Alaska 2021, 90 m, Zenodo https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.8423568, no licence declared, validation use only (row `zwieback-severity/` of 02.inputs/README.md).
sev <- terra::trim(terra::rast("02.inputs/zwieback-severity/merged_ref_h_c90c.tif"))
land_tif <- "02.inputs/derived/landscape_s1_levels.tif"
if (!file.exists(land_tif)) {
  eras <- list(pre = c("2014-10-01", "2017-01-01"), late = c("2019-06-01", "2021-09-01"))
  level <- function(o, e) s1_all$filter(ee$Filter$eq("relativeOrbitNumber_start", o))$filterDate(eras[[e]][1], eras[[e]][2])$map(function(img) flatten(img, "VV"))$mean()$rename(paste0("VV", o, "_", e))  # the mean slope-corrected VV of every scene of one orbit in one era
  img <- ee$Image$cat(unname(Map(level, rep(orbits, 2), rep(names(eras), each = 2))))$setDefaultProjection("EPSG:32605", NULL, 10)$reduceResolution(ee$Reducer$mean(), maxPixels = 256L)  # the 81 cells of 10 m averaged into each 90 m cell
  e <- as.vector(terra::ext(sev)); rows <- split(seq_len(nrow(sev)), ceiling(seq_len(nrow(sev)) / 10))
  tile_dir <- "02.inputs/derived/landscape_tiles"; dir.create(tile_dir, showWarnings = FALSE)
  for (r in rows) { f <- file.path(tile_dir, sprintf("rows_%03d.tif", min(r))); if (file.exists(f)) next  # ten rows per request, on the grid of the severity map, kept so that a failed run resumes
    url <- img$getDownloadURL(list(crs = "EPSG:32605", crs_transform = c(90, 0, e[1], 0, -90, e[4] - (min(r) - 1) * 90), dimensions = c(ncol(sev), length(r)), format = "GEO_TIFF", filePerBand = FALSE))
    for (attempt in 1:4) if (inherits(try(download.file(url, f, mode = "wb", quiet = TRUE), silent = TRUE), "try-error")) { unlink(f); Sys.sleep(30) } else break  # Earth Engine refuses a request now and then under load
    if (!file.exists(f)) stop("tile ", f, " did not download") }
  terra::writeRaster(terra::merge(terra::sprc(lapply(list.files(tile_dir, "^rows_.*\\.tif$", full.names = TRUE), terra::rast))), land_tif) }
lv <- terra::rast(land_tif); names(lv) <- paste0("VV", rep(orbits, 2), "_", rep(c("pre", "late"), each = 2))  # the GeoTIFF carries no band names
```

```{r}
#| label: landscape-test
#| echo: true
#| output: false
# USFS Forest Health Protection aerial detection survey damage areas, Alaska Region 10, all years.
# https://www.fs.usda.gov/foresthealth/docs/IDS_Data_for_Download/AK_Region10_AllYears.gdb.zip
con90 <- terra::project(terra::crop(conifer, terra::project(terra::as.polygons(terra::ext(lv), crs = "EPSG:32605"), terra::crs(conifer))), lv, method = "average")
surv <- sf::st_read("02.inputs/ids-region10/AK_Region10_AllYears.gdb", quiet = TRUE, query = "SELECT SURVEY_YEAR, Shape FROM DAMAGE_AREAS_FLAT_AllYears_AK_Rgn10 WHERE DCA_CODE = 11009 AND SURVEY_YEAR BETWEEN 2017 AND 2024")
in_surv <- terra::rasterize(terra::vect(sf::st_transform(surv, 32605)), lv, field = 1, background = 0)
land <- na.omit(data.frame(sev = terra::values(terra::resample(sev, lv, method = "near"))[, 1], terra::values(lv), conifer = terra::values(con90)[, 1], survey = terra::values(in_surv)[, 1]))
land$class <- ifelse(land$sev >= 0.01, "dead", ifelse(land$sev == 0 & land$conifer >= 5, "alive", NA)); lab_l <- !is.na(land$class); dead_l <- land$class == "dead"
forest_l <- land$conifer >= 5
land_auc <- sapply(c("VV65", "VV131"), function(b) c(level = auc(land[[paste0(b, "_pre")]][lab_l], dead_l[lab_l]), change = auc((land[[paste0(b, "_late")]] - land[[paste0(b, "_pre")]])[lab_l], dead_l[lab_l]),
  rho = cor(land[[paste0(b, "_pre")]][forest_l], land$sev[forest_l], method = "spearman"), survey = auc(land[[paste0(b, "_pre")]][forest_l], land$survey[forest_l] == 1)))
land_bins <- with(land[forest_l, ], tapply(VV131_pre, cut(sev, c(-1, 0, 0.01, 0.02, 0.05, 0.1, 1), c("0", "0 to 0.01", "0.01 to 0.02", "0.02 to 0.05", "0.05 to 0.1", "0.1 to 1")), mean))
```

```{r}
#| label: landscape-structure
#| echo: true
#| output: false
# ETH global canopy height 2020 at 10 m and its standard deviation (Lang et al. 2023), Earth Engine users/nlang/ETH_GlobalCanopyHeight_2020_10m_v1 and ETH_GlobalCanopyHeightSD_2020_10m_v1.
# https://doi.org/10.1038/s41559-023-02206-6 and https://gee-community-catalog.org/projects/canopy/
# USGS 3D Elevation Program 10 m terrain, the Alaska 5 m interferometric radar terrain model resampled, Earth Engine USGS/3DEP/10m_collection.
# https://developers.google.com/earth-engine/datasets/catalog/USGS_3DEP_10m_collection
# Copernicus GLO-30 surface model, Earth Engine COPERNICUS/DEM/GLO30_2024_1.
# https://developers.google.com/earth-engine/datasets/catalog/COPERNICUS_DEM_GLO30_2024_1
# ArcticDEM version 4 surface model mosaic at 2 m, Earth Engine UMN/PGC/ArcticDEM/V4/2m_mosaic.
# https://developers.google.com/earth-engine/datasets/catalog/UMN_PGC_ArcticDEM_V4_2m_mosaic
# JAXA ALOS PALSAR and PALSAR-2 yearly mosaics at 25 m, Earth Engine JAXA/ALOS/PALSAR/YEARLY/SAR.
# https://developers.google.com/earth-engine/datasets/catalog/JAXA_ALOS_PALSAR_YEARLY_SAR
struct_tif <- "02.inputs/derived/landscape_structure.tif"
if (!file.exists(struct_tif)) {
  at <- function(img, m) img$setDefaultProjection("EPSG:32605", NULL, m)$reduceResolution(ee$Reducer$mean(), maxPixels = 1024L)  # declare the source cell size, then average the cells inside each 90 m cell
  gamma0 <- function(img) img$select(c("HH", "HV"))$pow(2)$multiply(10^-8.3)$updateMask(img$select("qa")$eq(255))  # digital number to linear gamma0, 10 log10(DN^2) - 83 dB, land cells only
  lband <- function(y1, y2, e) ee$ImageCollection("JAXA/ALOS/PALSAR/YEARLY/SAR")$filterDate(paste0(y1, "-01-01"), paste0(y2, "-12-31"))$map(gamma0)$mean()$rename(paste0(c("HH", "HV"), "_", e))  # the years are filtered before the arithmetic, which drops the date stamp
  img <- ee$Image$cat(list(
    at(ee$Image("users/nlang/ETH_GlobalCanopyHeight_2020_10m_v1")$rename("eth"), 10), at(ee$Image("users/nlang/ETH_GlobalCanopyHeightSD_2020_10m_v1")$rename("eth_sd"), 10),
    at(ee$ImageCollection("USGS/3DEP/10m_collection")$mosaic()$select("elevation")$rename("dtm"), 10),
    at(ee$ImageCollection("COPERNICUS/DEM/GLO30_2024_1")$mosaic()$select("DEM")$rename("glo"), 30),
    at(ee$Image("UMN/PGC/ArcticDEM/V4/2m_mosaic")$select("elevation")$rename("arctic"), 10),
    at(lband(2015, 2016, "pre"), 25), at(lband(2019, 2020, "late"), 25)))
  e <- as.vector(terra::ext(sev)); rows <- split(seq_len(nrow(sev)), ceiling(seq_len(nrow(sev)) / 60))
  tile_dir <- "02.inputs/derived/landscape_tiles"; dir.create(tile_dir, showWarnings = FALSE)
  for (r in rows) { f <- file.path(tile_dir, sprintf("structure_%03d.tif", min(r))); if (file.exists(f)) next  # sixty rows per request, on the grid of the severity map
    url <- img$getDownloadURL(list(crs = "EPSG:32605", crs_transform = c(90, 0, e[1], 0, -90, e[4] - (min(r) - 1) * 90), dimensions = c(ncol(sev), length(r)), format = "GEO_TIFF", filePerBand = FALSE))
    for (attempt in 1:4) if (inherits(try(download.file(url, f, mode = "wb", quiet = TRUE), silent = TRUE), "try-error")) { unlink(f); Sys.sleep(30) } else break
    if (!file.exists(f)) stop("tile ", f, " did not download") }
  terra::writeRaster(terra::merge(terra::sprc(lapply(list.files(tile_dir, "^structure_.*\\.tif$", full.names = TRUE), terra::rast))), struct_tif) }
st <- terra::rast(struct_tif); names(st) <- c("eth", "eth_sd", "dtm", "glo", "arctic", "HH_pre", "HV_pre", "HH_late", "HV_late")
```

```{r}
#| label: structure-test
#| echo: true
#| output: false
sv <- as.data.frame(terra::values(st))[as.integer(rownames(land)), ]  # the same cells as `land`, which na.omit left numbered by cell
sv$arctic[!is.na(sv$arctic) & sv$arctic <= 0] <- NA  # the mosaic covers half the strip
land <- cbind(land, height_eth = sv$eth, height_eth_sd = sv$eth_sd, height_glo = sv$glo - sv$dtm, height_arctic = sv$arctic - sv$dtm,  # surface model minus terrain model, an offset-free canopy height
  HV_pre = 10 * log10(sv$HV_pre), HH_pre = 10 * log10(sv$HH_pre), HV_change = 10 * log10(sv$HV_late / sv$HV_pre))
auc_ok <- function(x, y) { ok <- !is.na(x); auc(x[ok], y[ok]) }
struct <- sapply(c("height_eth", "height_glo", "height_arctic", "HV_pre", "HH_pre", "HV_change", "VV65_pre", "VV131_pre"), function(v) { x <- land[[v]]; ok <- !is.na(x)
  c(n = sum(ok & lab_l), AUC = auc_ok(x[lab_l], dead_l[lab_l]), dead = mean(x[ok & lab_l & dead_l]), alive = mean(x[ok & lab_l & !dead_l]),
    rho_sev = cor(x[ok & forest_l], land$sev[ok & forest_l], method = "spearman"), rho_VV65 = cor(x[ok & forest_l], land$VV65_pre[ok & forest_l], method = "spearman"), rho_VV131 = cor(x[ok & forest_l], land$VV131_pre[ok & forest_l], method = "spearman")) })
d <- na.omit(data.frame(y = dead_l[lab_l], land[lab_l, c("height_eth", "height_glo", "HV_pre", "HH_pre", "VV65_pre", "VV131_pre")]))
fit_auc <- function(f) auc(predict(glm(f, family = binomial, data = d)), d$y)  # a logistic fit on the same cells, so the question is only whether a second source adds rank
added <- sapply(list(height = y ~ height_eth + height_glo, c_band = y ~ VV65_pre + VV131_pre, l_band = y ~ HV_pre + HH_pre, c_band_height = y ~ VV65_pre + VV131_pre + height_eth + height_glo, l_band_height = y ~ HV_pre + HH_pre + height_eth + height_glo, all = y ~ VV65_pre + VV131_pre + HV_pre + HH_pre + height_eth + height_glo), fit_auc)
struct_bins <- with(land[forest_l, ], sapply(list(height_eth = height_eth, height_glo = height_glo, HV_pre = HV_pre), function(x) tapply(x, cut(sev, c(-1, 0, 0.01, 0.02, 0.05, 0.1, 1), c("0", "0 to 0.01", "0.01 to 0.02", "0.02 to 0.05", "0.05 to 0.1", "0.1 to 1")), mean, na.rm = TRUE)))
write.csv(struct, "03.outputs/landscape_structure.csv")  # read by the abstract, which renders before this chunk
```
