```{r}
#| label: landcover-test
#| echo: true
#| output: false
cover <- t(sapply(split(which(lab_l), land$evt[lab_l]), function(i) { y <- dead_l[i]; big <- sum(y) >= 100 && sum(!y) >= 100  # dead and living cells by vegetation class, and whether height still ranks them inside one class
  c(dead = sum(y), living = sum(!y), height_dead = mean(land$height_eth[i][y], na.rm = TRUE), height_living = mean(land$height_eth[i][!y], na.rm = TRUE),
    AUC_height = if (big) auc_ok(land$height_eth[i], y) else NA, AUC_VV65 = if (big) auc_ok(land$VV65_pre[i], y) else NA, AUC_HV = if (big) auc_ok(land$HV_pre[i], y) else NA) }))
cover <- cover[order(-(cover[, "dead"] + cover[, "living"])), ]
dc <- na.omit(data.frame(y = dead_l[lab_l], cls = land$evt[lab_l], land[lab_l, c("height_eth", "VV65_pre")]))
cover_added <- sapply(list(class = y ~ cls, height = y ~ height_eth, class_height = y ~ cls + height_eth, class_c_band = y ~ cls + VV65_pre), function(f) auc(predict(glm(f, family = binomial, data = dc)), dc$y))  # does height add rank once the class is known
```

Because the `r format(nrow(stands), big.mark = " ")` stands were chosen by @Zwieback_2024, the first hypothesis was then tested across their severity map, a strip `r ncol(sev) * 90 / 1000` by `r round(nrow(sev) * 90 / 1000)` km. The mean slope-corrected VV of every scene of each orbit in the two periods, the three canopy heights, and the L-band mosaics of 2015 and 2016 were averaged into the 90 m cells of the map. Of the `r format(nrow(land), big.mark = " ")` cells with values, a cell was dead at a severity of 0.01 or more and living at 0 with conifer top cover of 5 per cent or more. Each source was scored as for the stands, and by Spearman's rank correlation with severity over the forest cells. Logistic regressions on the cells with every source present tested whether a second source improved the ranking given by the first. The level was scored against the survey polygons of 2017 to 2024 rasterized onto the same cells. The LANDFIRE class of each cell tested whether the height contrast was present within a cover class or was a contrast between host and non-host.

## Statewide map

```{r}
#| label: statewide-angle
#| echo: true
#| output: false
# Sentinel-1 GRD and the ETH canopy height 2020, read above; US Census TIGER/Line 2018 state boundaries, Earth Engine TIGER/2018/States (row `TIGER/2018/States` of 02.inputs/README.md).
# https://developers.google.com/earth-engine/datasets/catalog/TIGER_2018_States
angle_csv <- "03.outputs/statewide_angle.csv"
ak <- ee$FeatureCollection("TIGER/2018/States")$filter(ee$Filter$eq("NAME", "Alaska"))$geometry()
ak_box <- ee$Geometry$Rectangle(c(-170, 54, -129, 71.5), "EPSG:4326", FALSE)  # the forested state without the far Aleutians, which cross the antimeridian
eth10 <- ee$Image("users/nlang/ETH_GlobalCanopyHeight_2020_10m_v1")$select(0)$rename("height")
forest10 <- eth10$gte(5)  # forest is a 10 m cell with canopy height of 5 m or more
s1_pre <- s1_all$filterBounds(ak)$filterDate("2014-10-01", "2017-01-01")  # every VV scene over Alaska from October 2014 to December 2016
if (!file.exists(angle_csv)) {  # how slope-corrected VV falls with incidence angle over forest, fitted inside each of 150 scenes drawn at random, so that scenes of every orbit can be pooled
  fits <- s1_pre$randomColumn("r", 20261014L)$sort("r")$limit(150L)$map(function(img) { img <- ee$Image(img)  # flatten names its one band "constant", so it is renamed before the fit
    ee$Feature(NULL, flatten(img, "VV")$rename("VV")$addBands(img$select("angle"))$updateMask(forest10)$select(list("angle", "VV"))$reduceRegion(ee$Reducer$linearFit(), img$geometry(), 300, maxPixels = 1e9, tileScale = 4))$set(list(orbit = img$get("relativeOrbitNumber_start"), date = img$date()$format("YYYY-MM-dd"))) })
  fits <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(fits$getInfo()$features, function(f) Filter(Negate(is.null), f$properties)))
  write.csv(data.frame(fits, slope_median = median(fits$scale, na.rm = TRUE)), angle_csv, row.names = FALSE) }
angle_fit <- read.csv(angle_csv); angle_slope <- angle_fit$slope_median[1]  # dB per degree of incidence angle
```

```{r}
#| label: statewide
#| echo: true
#| output: false
task_csv <- "03.outputs/statewide_task.csv"; asset_id <- paste0("projects/", ee_project, "/assets/spruce_susceptibility_alaska_90m")
norm_vv <- function(img) flatten(img, "VV", smooth = FALSE)$rename("VV")$subtract(img$select("angle")$subtract(38)$multiply(angle_slope))$rename("VV")  # slope-corrected VV brought to the mid-swath incidence angle of 38 degrees; the mean over scenes replaces the 3 by 3 filter
lin <- function(img) ee$Image$constant(10)$pow(img$divide(10))$rename("VV")  # decibels to linear power; the constant image names the result "constant" unless renamed
pre_vv <- s1_pre$map(norm_vv)
pooled_lin <- pre_vv$map(lin)$reduce(ee$Reducer$mean()$combine(ee$Reducer$count(), sharedInputs = TRUE))  # the mean of every scene in linear power and the scene count in one pass
pooled_s1 <- ee$Image$cat(list(pooled_lin$select("VV_mean")$log10()$multiply(10)$rename("VV"), pooled_lin$select("VV_count")$rename("scenes")))  # VV in decibels and the scene count, computed at whatever scale is requested, 90 m throughout this study, so each scene is read at the 90 m level of its image pyramid
at90 <- function(img, crs = "EPSG:3338") img$setDefaultProjection(crs, NULL, 10)$reduceResolution(ee$Reducer$mean(), maxPixels = 256L)  # the 10 m cells averaged into each 90 m cell
pooled_image <- function(crs = "EPSG:3338") { s <- at90(ee$Image$cat(list(eth10, forest10$unmask(0)$rename("forest"))), crs)  # canopy height as the cell mean and forest as the share of the cell, both from 10 m
  ee$Image$cat(list(pooled_s1, s))$updateMask(s$select("forest")$gt(0)) }
pooled <- pooled_image()
if (!file.exists(task_csv)) {  # the 90 m statewide map, exported once to an asset of the Earth Engine project, where the managers and the figure below read it
  task <- ee$batch$Export$image$toAsset(image = pooled$multiply(100)$round()$toInt16(), description = "spruce_susceptibility_alaska_90m", assetId = asset_id, region = ak_box, crs = "EPSG:3338", crsTransform = list(90, 0, 0, 0, -90, 0), maxPixels = 1e10, pyramidingPolicy = list(.default = "mean"), shardSize = 64L)  # a 64-cell shard reads a 576 by 576 window of 10 m cells; the default 256 exceeded the worker memory limit at 32 per cent on 2026-10-14
  task$start(); write.csv(data.frame(task = task$id, asset = asset_id, started = format(Sys.time(), "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M")), task_csv, row.names = FALSE) }
```

if (!file.exists(pooled_tif)) {  # the statewide product on the cells of the severity map, ten rows per request, so that the map is validated exactly as it is made
  img <- pooled_image("EPSG:32605"); e <- as.vector(terra::ext(sev)); rows <- split(seq_len(nrow(sev)), ceiling(seq_len(nrow(sev)) / 10))
  tile_dir <- "02.inputs/derived/landscape_tiles"; dir.create(tile_dir, showWarnings = FALSE)
  for (r in rows) { f <- file.path(tile_dir, sprintf("pooled_%03d.tif", min(r))); if (file.exists(f)) next
    for (attempt in 1:6) { ok <- !inherits(try({ url <- img$getDownloadURL(list(crs = "EPSG:32605", crs_transform = c(90, 0, e[1], 0, -90, e[4] - (min(r) - 1) * 90), dimensions = c(ncol(sev), length(r)), format = "GEO_TIFF", filePerBand = FALSE))
      download.file(url, f, mode = "wb", quiet = TRUE) }, silent = TRUE), "try-error"); if (ok) break; unlink(f); Sys.sleep(30) }  # the request itself times out under load now and then, so it is retried with the download
    if (!file.exists(f)) stop("tile ", f, " did not download") }
  terra::writeRaster(terra::merge(terra::sprc(lapply(list.files(tile_dir, "^pooled_.*\\.tif$", full.names = TRUE), terra::rast))), pooled_tif) }
pl <- terra::rast(pooled_tif); names(pl) <- c("VV_pooled", "scenes", "height_pooled", "forest")  # the GeoTIFF carries no band names
pv <- as.data.frame(terra::values(pl))[as.integer(rownames(land)), ]; land$VV_pooled <- pv$VV_pooled; land$scenes <- pv$scenes
youden <- function(x, y) { ok <- !is.na(x); x <- x[ok]; y <- y[ok]; th <- sort(unique(round(x, 2))); j <- sapply(th, function(t) mean(x[y] >= t) + mean(x[!y] < t) - 1); th[which.max(j)] }  # the threshold with the largest sum of the two correct rates
pooled_strip <- c(n = sum(lab_l & !is.na(land$VV_pooled)), AUC = auc_ok(land$VV_pooled[lab_l], dead_l[lab_l]), AUC_height = auc_ok(land$height_eth[lab_l], dead_l[lab_l]), AUC_survey = auc_ok(land$VV_pooled[forest_l], land$survey[forest_l] == 1),
  dead = mean(land$VV_pooled[lab_l & dead_l], na.rm = TRUE), alive = mean(land$VV_pooled[lab_l & !dead_l], na.rm = TRUE), scenes = median(land$scenes[forest_l], na.rm = TRUE), rho_height = cor(land$VV_pooled[forest_l], land$height_eth[forest_l], method = "spearman", use = "complete.obs"),
  thr_VV = youden(land$VV_pooled[lab_l], dead_l[lab_l]), thr_height = youden(land$height_eth[lab_l], dead_l[lab_l]))
pooled_strip["sens_VV"] <- mean(land$VV_pooled[lab_l & dead_l] >= pooled_strip["thr_VV"], na.rm = TRUE); pooled_strip["spec_VV"] <- mean(land$VV_pooled[lab_l & !dead_l] < pooled_strip["thr_VV"], na.rm = TRUE)  # the two correct rates at the threshold
pooled_strip["n_dead"] <- sum(lab_l & dead_l & !is.na(land$VV_pooled)); pooled_strip["n_alive"] <- sum(lab_l & !dead_l & !is.na(land$VV_pooled)); pooled_strip["acc_VV"] <- mean((land$VV_pooled[lab_l] >= pooled_strip["thr_VV"]) == dead_l[lab_l], na.rm = TRUE)  # the share of all labelled cells classed correctly, the overall accuracy
write.csv(data.frame(t(pooled_strip)), "03.outputs/statewide_strip.csv", row.names = FALSE)  # read by the abstract, which renders before this chunk
```

For the second hypothesis, every Sentinel-1 VV scene over Alaska from October 2014 to December 2016 was pooled into one map. Slope-corrected VV falls with incidence angle across a swath, so the fall was fitted as the slope of VV on angle over the forest cells of 150 scenes drawn at random, at 300 m, and the median over the `r sum(!is.na(angle_fit$scale))` scenes that covered forest, `r sprintf("%.3f", angle_slope)` dB per degree, brought every scene to the mid-swath angle of 38 degrees. Forest was a 10 m cell with an ETH Zurich canopy height of 5 m or more. The product was computed at 90 m on the Alaska Albers grid, each scene read at the 90 m level of its image pyramid and averaged over scenes in linear power, with the scene count, the mean canopy height, and the forest share of the 10 m cells as further bands, and was exported as the Earth Engine asset named in the code. It was validated as made, read on the cells of the severity map and scored against the dead and living cells, the survey, and the ETH Zurich height. The threshold that maximized the index of @Youden_1950, the sum of the two correct rates less one, `r sprintf("%.2f", pooled_strip["thr_VV"])` dB, defined a susceptible cell in everything that follows, the same rule gave `r sprintf("%.1f", pooled_strip["thr_height"])` m on the height map, and the two correct rates and the overall accuracy, the share of all labelled cells classed correctly, were computed at that threshold.

```{r}
#| label: diagnostics
#| echo: true
#| output: false
diag_csv <- c(sep = "03.outputs/diagnostics_separability.csv", fit = "03.outputs/diagnostics_fit.csv")
M_index <- function(x, y) abs(mean(x[y]) - mean(x[!y])) / (sd(x[y]) + sd(x[!y]))  # Kaufman and Remer (1994), the difference of the class means over the sum of their standard deviations; above 1 is good separability
stars <- function(p) ifelse(is.na(p), "", ifelse(p <= 0.0001, "****", ifelse(p <= 0.001, "***", ifelse(p <= 0.01, "**", ifelse(p <= 0.05, "*", "")))))
confusion <- function(hit, y) { tp <- sum(hit & y); fp <- sum(hit & !y); fn <- sum(!hit & y); tn <- sum(!hit & !y); n <- length(y); po <- (tp + tn) / n  # the confusion matrix of a hard classification, read as Murphy et al. (2026) Table 8
  pe <- ((tp + fp) * (tp + fn) + (fn + tn) * (fp + tn)) / n^2; ci <- binom.test(tp + tn, n)$conf.int
  c(kappa = (po - pe) / (1 - pe), com_dead = fp / (tp + fp), com_living = fn / (fn + tn), om_dead = fn / (tp + fn), om_living = fp / (fp + tn), OA = po, OA_lo = ci[1], OA_hi = ci[2]) }
score_source <- function(x, y, thr = NULL, M = TRUE) { ok <- !is.na(x); x <- x[ok]; y <- y[ok]; if (is.null(thr)) thr <- youden(x, y)  # one source or score against the label, at its Youden threshold unless one is given
  ci <- as.numeric(pROC::ci.auc(pROC::roc(as.integer(y), x, quiet = TRUE, direction = "<"), method = "delong"))
  c(dead = sum(y), living = sum(!y), M = if (M) M_index(x, y) else NA, p_M = if (M) wilcox.test(x[y], x[!y])$p.value else NA, AUC = ci[2], AUC_lo = ci[1], AUC_hi = ci[3], thr = thr, confusion(x >= thr, y)) }
strip_sources <- c(VV_pooled = "Sentinel-1 VV, statewide product", VV65_pre = "Sentinel-1 VV, ascending orbit 65", VV131_pre = "Sentinel-1 VV, descending orbit 131", height_eth = "ETH canopy height 2020", height_glo = "GLO-30 surface minus terrain", height_arctic = "ArcticDEM surface minus terrain", HV_pre = "PALSAR L-band HV", HH_pre = "PALSAR L-band HH")
if (!all(file.exists(diag_csv))) {
  spt <- read.csv(strain_csv, colClasses = c(roi = "character")); spt$label <- ifelse(spt$dead >= 0.01, TRUE, ifelse(spt$dead == 0 & spt$conifer >= 5, FALSE, NA))
  net_te <- sp[sp$design == "VV_2014" & sp$set == "training" & !is.na(sp$label), ]; net_te <- net_te[order(net_te$stand), ]; net_tr <- spt[spt$design == "VV_2014" & !is.na(spt$label), ]  # the network's held-out folds, in stand order, and its training stands
  sep <- rbind(t(sapply(names(strip_sources), function(v) score_source(land[[v]][lab_l], dead_l[lab_l]))), network = score_source(net_te$p_dead, net_te$label, thr = 0.5, M = FALSE))
  write.csv(data.frame(source = c(strip_sources, "Temporal network, crown labels, held-out folds"), label = c(rep("Severity map", length(strip_sources)), "Crown labels"), sep, row.names = NULL), diag_csv["sep"], row.names = FALSE)
  dd <- na.omit(data.frame(cell = as.integer(rownames(land))[lab_l], y = dead_l[lab_l], land[lab_l, c("VV_pooled", "VV65_pre", "VV131_pre", "height_eth", "height_glo", "HV_pre", "HH_pre")]))  # the labelled cells with every source but the ArcticDEM, which covers half the strip
  xy <- terra::xyFromCell(lv, dd$cell); lw <- spdep::nb2listw(spdep::knn2nb(spdep::knearneigh(xy, k = 8)))  # the cell coordinates, their eight nearest neighbours for Moran's I
  set.seed(20261018); ac <- blockCV::cv_spatial_autocor(r = c(pl$VV_pooled, lv$VV65_pre, lv$VV131_pre, st$eth, st$glo - st$dtm, 10 * log10(st$HV_pre)), num_sample = 5000L, plot = FALSE, progress = FALSE)  # the autocorrelation range of the sources, the block size of the folds
  blk <- min(max(ac$range, 1000), 15000); fd <- blockCV::cv_spatial(x = sf::st_as_sf(data.frame(xy), coords = c("x", "y"), crs = 32605), k = 5L, size = blk, selection = "random", seed = 20261018, progress = FALSE, report = FALSE, plot = FALSE)$folds_ids
  fit_diag <- function(f, data, folds) { m <- glm(f, family = binomial, data = data); p <- fitted(m); y <- data$y; e <- y - p; n <- nrow(data)
    r2 <- (1 - exp((m$deviance - m$null.deviance) / n)) / (1 - exp(-m$null.deviance / n)); p_lr <- pchisq(m$null.deviance - m$deviance, m$df.null - m$df.residual, lower.tail = FALSE)  # Nagelkerke's R2 and the likelihood ratio test against the null fit
    grp <- cut(p, unique(quantile(p, seq(0, 1, length.out = 11))), include.lowest = TRUE); o <- tapply(y, grp, sum); ex <- tapply(p, grp, sum); ng <- tapply(p, grp, length); hl <- sum((o - ex)^2 / (ex * (1 - ex / ng)))  # Hosmer-Lemeshow over ten groups of fitted probability
    mi <- spdep::moran.test(e, lw, randomisation = TRUE)
    cv <- lapply(sort(unique(folds)), function(k) { mk <- glm(f, family = binomial, data = data[folds != k, ]); pk <- predict(mk, data[folds == k, ], type = "response")  # each fold held out in turn
      list(train = sqrt(mean((data$y[folds != k] - fitted(mk))^2)), test = sqrt(mean((data$y[folds == k] - pk)^2)), p = pk, y = data$y[folds == k]) })
    tr <- mean(sapply(cv, `[[`, "train")); te <- mean(sapply(cv, `[[`, "test")); pt <- unlist(lapply(cv, `[[`, "p")); yt <- unlist(lapply(cv, `[[`, "y"))
    c(R2 = r2, p_R2 = p_lr, HL = hl, p_HL = pchisq(hl, nlevels(grp) - 2, lower.tail = FALSE), Brier = mean(e^2), RMSE = sqrt(mean(e^2)), rRMSE = 100 * sqrt(mean(e^2)) / mean(y), MAE = mean(abs(e)), RMSE_train = tr, RMSE_test = te, ratio = te / tr, U_bias = (mean(pt) - mean(yt))^2 / mean((pt - yt)^2), I = unname(mi$estimate[1]), p_I = mi$p.value, DW = sum(diff(e)^2) / sum(e^2)) }
  fit_forms <- list("Sentinel-1 VV, statewide product" = y ~ VV_pooled, "Sentinel-1 VV, ascending orbit 65" = y ~ VV65_pre, "Sentinel-1 VV, descending orbit 131" = y ~ VV131_pre, "ETH canopy height 2020" = y ~ height_eth, "GLO-30 surface minus terrain" = y ~ height_glo, "PALSAR L-band HV" = y ~ HV_pre,
    "Two canopy heights" = y ~ height_eth + height_glo, "Two C-band orbits" = y ~ VV65_pre + VV131_pre, "L-band HV and HH" = y ~ HV_pre + HH_pre, "C-band and heights" = y ~ VV65_pre + VV131_pre + height_eth + height_glo, "L-band and heights" = y ~ HV_pre + HH_pre + height_eth + height_glo, "All six sources" = y ~ VV65_pre + VV131_pre + HV_pre + HH_pre + height_eth + height_glo)  # the single sources and the six fits of the structure test
  net_fold <- sapply(1:5, function(f) c(train = sqrt(mean((net_tr$label[net_tr$fold_model == f] - net_tr$p_dead[net_tr$fold_model == f])^2)), test = sqrt(mean((net_te$label[net_te$fold == f] - net_te$p_dead[net_te$fold == f])^2))))  # each fold's network on its training stands and on its held-out fold
  e_net <- net_te$label - net_te$p_dead; mi_net <- spdep::moran.test(e_net, spdep::nb2listw(spdep::knn2nb(spdep::knearneigh(as.matrix(stands[match(net_te$stand, stands$stand), c("x", "y")]), k = 8))), randomisation = TRUE)
  net_fit <- c(R2 = NA, p_R2 = NA, HL = NA, p_HL = NA, Brier = mean(e_net^2), RMSE = sqrt(mean(e_net^2)), rRMSE = 100 * sqrt(mean(e_net^2)) / mean(net_te$label), MAE = mean(abs(e_net)), RMSE_train = mean(net_fold["train", ]), RMSE_test = mean(net_fold["test", ]), ratio = mean(net_fold["test", ]) / mean(net_fold["train", ]),
    U_bias = (mean(net_te$p_dead) - mean(net_te$label))^2 / mean(e_net^2), I = unname(mi_net$estimate[1]), p_I = mi_net$p.value, DW = sum(diff(e_net)^2) / sum(e_net^2))
  write.csv(data.frame(model = c(names(fit_forms), "Temporal network, crown labels, held-out folds"), n = c(rep(nrow(dd), length(fit_forms)), nrow(net_te)), rbind(t(sapply(fit_forms, fit_diag, data = dd, folds = fd)), net_fit), range_m = ac$range, block_m = blk, row.names = NULL), diag_csv["fit"], row.names = FALSE) }
diag_sep <- read.csv(diag_csv["sep"]); diag_fit <- read.csv(diag_csv["fit"])
diag_sep$source <- sub("^Temporal network", "Temp network", diag_sep$source); diag_fit$model <- sub("^Temporal network", "Temp network", diag_fit$model)  # the row label Seamus shortened in Word on 2026-10-18; the saved tables keep the long form
dsev <- diag_sep[diag_sep$label == "Severity map", ]; dnet_sep <- diag_sep[diag_sep$label == "Crown labels", ]; dfit <- diag_fit[!is.na(diag_fit$R2), ]; dnet_fit <- diag_fit[is.na(diag_fit$R2), ]  # the strip sources, the network, the logistic fits and the network again, as the text reads them
```

Every source on the severity map, and the network on the crown labels, was then scored by the metrics of @Murphy_2026. Before any model was fitted, the separability of the dead from the living cells on each source was measured by the index M of @Kaufman_1994, the difference of the two class means over the sum of their standard deviations, with M above 1 taken as good separability, and tested with the Wilcoxon rank-sum test. The area under the curve carried the 95 per cent confidence interval of @DeLong_1988, and at the Youden threshold of each source the confusion matrix gave Cohen's kappa [@Cohen_1960], the commission and omission error of each class, and the overall accuracy with its exact binomial 95 per cent confidence interval. The threshold classifier and the network assumed no distribution of the backscatter, while the logistic fits were parametric binomial regressions, each scored by Nagelkerke's R² [@Nagelkerke_1991] with the likelihood ratio test, the Hosmer-Lemeshow test over ten groups [@Hosmer_1980], the Brier score [@Brier_1950], the root mean square error, the same error relative to the mean of the label, the mean absolute error, Moran's I of the residuals over the eight nearest cells [@Moran_1950] and the Durbin-Watson statistic of the residuals in cell order [@Durbin_1950]. Overfitting was the root mean square error of the held-out folds over that of the training folds, rejected above 1.1 as in @Murphy_2026, and systematic bias the bias share of Theil's U [@Theil_1966] on the held-out predictions, both over five spatial folds dealt by blockCV in blocks of `r sprintf("%.0f", diag_fit$block_m[1] / 1000)` km, no smaller than the `r sprintf("%.2f", diag_fit$range_m[1] / 1000)` km autocorrelation range of the sources on the strip. The network's ratio used the predictions of each fold's network on its own training stands.

## Regional validation

```{r}
#| label: matsu
#| echo: true
#| output: false
# US Census TIGER/Line 2018 county boundaries, Earth Engine TIGER/2018/Counties, GEOID 02170 the Matanuska-Susitna Borough (row `TIGER/2018/Counties` of 02.inputs/README.md).
# https://developers.google.com/earth-engine/datasets/catalog/TIGER_2018_Counties
# USFS Forest Health Protection aerial detection survey, Alaska Region 10, all years, the damage areas and the surveyed areas.
# https://www.fs.usda.gov/foresthealth/docs/IDS_Data_for_Download/AK_Region10_AllYears.gdb.zip
# ABoVE conifer top cover 2020 (Macander and Nelson 2022), ORNL DAAC https://doi.org/10.3334/ORNLDAAC/2032, read above as `conifer`; it covers nine tenths of the borough.
# The height and radar sources are those of the landscape chunks above, ETH canopy height 2020, USGS 3DEP 10 m terrain, Copernicus GLO-30, ArcticDEM version 4, JAXA ALOS PALSAR yearly mosaics 2007 to 2010 and 2015 to 2016, and Sentinel-1 GRD.
gdb <- "02.inputs/ids-region10/AK_Region10_AllYears.gdb"
predictor_image <- function(crs = "EPSG:3338") {  # the pre-outbreak height and radar sources of the strip, averaged into the 90 m cells of the given grid
  at3 <- function(img, m) img$setDefaultProjection(crs, NULL, m)$reduceResolution(ee$Reducer$mean(), maxPixels = 4096L)  # declare the source cell size, then average the cells inside each 90 m cell
  gamma0 <- function(img) img$select(c("HH", "HV"))$pow(2)$multiply(10^-8.3)$updateMask(img$select("qa")$eq(255))
  lband <- function(y1, y2, e) ee$ImageCollection("JAXA/ALOS/PALSAR/YEARLY/SAR")$filterDate(paste0(y1, "-01-01"), paste0(y2, "-12-31"))$map(gamma0)$mean()$rename(paste0(c("HH", "HV"), "_", e))
  vv_pre <- function(o) s1_all$filter(ee$Filter$eq("relativeOrbitNumber_start", o))$filterDate("2014-10-01", "2017-01-01")$map(function(img) flatten(img, "VV"))$mean()$rename(paste0("VV", o))  # the same era as the strip
  ee$Image$cat(list(at3(ee$Image("users/nlang/ETH_GlobalCanopyHeight_2020_10m_v1")$rename("eth"), 10), at3(ee$ImageCollection("USGS/3DEP/10m_collection")$mosaic()$select("elevation")$rename("dtm"), 10),
    at3(ee$ImageCollection("COPERNICUS/DEM/GLO30_2024_1")$mosaic()$select("DEM")$rename("glo"), 30), at3(ee$Image("UMN/PGC/ArcticDEM/V4/2m_mosaic")$select("elevation")$rename("arctic"), 10),
    at3(lband(2007, 2010, "2007"), 25), at3(lband(2015, 2016, "2015"), 25), at3(vv_pre(orbits[1]), 10), at3(vv_pre(orbits[2]), 10))) }
pull_cells <- function(smp, prefix, buffer = 0, crs = "EPSG:3338", img = predictor_image(crs)) {  # the 90 m cell of `img` holding each point, or the mean of the cells within `buffer` metres of it, a thousand points per request
  tile_dir <- "02.inputs/derived/landscape_tiles"; dir.create(tile_dir, showWarnings = FALSE)
  for (b in split(seq_len(nrow(smp)), ceiling(seq_len(nrow(smp)) / 1000))) { f <- file.path(tile_dir, sprintf("%s_%05d.csv", prefix, min(b))); if (file.exists(f)) next  # kept so that a failed run resumes
    pts <- ee$FeatureCollection(lapply(b, function(i) list(type = "Feature", geometry = list(type = "Point", coordinates = c(smp$lon[i], smp$lat[i])), properties = list(cell = smp$cell[i]))))
    if (buffer > 0) pts <- pts$map(function(ft) ee$Feature(ft)$buffer(buffer))
    for (attempt in 1:4) { z <- try(img$reduceRegions(collection = pts, reducer = if (buffer > 0) ee$Reducer$mean() else ee$Reducer$first(), scale = 90, crs = crs, tileScale = 16)$getInfo()$features, silent = TRUE); if (inherits(z, "try-error")) Sys.sleep(30) else break }
    if (inherits(z, "try-error")) stop("batch ", f, " did not return: ", z); write.csv(dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(z, function(q) Filter(Negate(is.null), q$properties))), f, row.names = FALSE) }
  got <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(list.files(tile_dir, sprintf("^%s_[0-9]+\\.csv$", prefix), full.names = TRUE), read.csv)); got[match(smp$cell, got$cell), setdiff(names(got), "cell")] }
region_sample <- function(geoids, csv, img = predictor_image(), prefix = paste0("region_", geoids[1]), n = 20000, reach = 10000, seed = 20261013) {  # one row per sampled 90 m cell of one or more boroughs, dead or living by the survey, with the bands of `img` read from Earth Engine
  if (file.exists(csv)) return(read.csv(csv))
  fc <- ee$FeatureCollection("TIGER/2018/Counties")$filter(ee$Filter$inList("GEOID", as.list(geoids))); tmp <- tempfile(fileext = ".geojson"); download.file(fc$getDownloadURL("geojson"), tmp, quiet = TRUE)
  bor <- sf::st_union(sf::st_transform(sf::st_read(tmp, quiet = TRUE), 3338)); e <- sf::st_bbox(bor)
  r <- terra::rast(terra::ext(floor(e$xmin / 90) * 90, ceiling(e$xmax / 90) * 90, floor(e$ymin / 90) * 90, ceiling(e$ymax / 90) * 90), resolution = 90, crs = "EPSG:3338")  # 90 m cells of the Alaska Albers grid with its origin at zero, the grid Earth Engine samples below
  sb <- sf::st_read(gdb, quiet = TRUE, query = "SELECT SURVEY_YEAR, HOST_CODE, PERCENT_MID, Shape FROM DAMAGE_AREAS_FLAT_AllYears_AK_Rgn10 WHERE DCA_CODE = 11009 AND SURVEY_YEAR >= 2014")
  sb <- sb[lengths(sf::st_intersects(sb, sf::st_as_sf(terra::as.polygons(terra::ext(r), crs = "EPSG:3338")))) > 0, ]; ws <- sb[sb$HOST_CODE == 94 & sb$SURVEY_YEAR %in% 2016:2024, ]  # spruce beetle on white spruce, 2016 to 2024
  year <- terra::setValues(r, NA_integer_); for (y in 2024:2016) year <- terra::rasterize(terra::vect(ws[ws$SURVEY_YEAR == y, ]), year, field = y, update = TRUE)  # the first survey year in which a cell lay inside a white spruce polygon
  pct <- terra::setValues(r, 0); for (p in sort(unique(ws$PERCENT_MID))) pct <- terra::rasterize(terra::vect(ws[ws$PERCENT_MID == p, ]), pct, field = p, update = TRUE)  # the highest mid-point of the polygon's mortality class over the years
  any_sb <- terra::rasterize(terra::vect(sb), r, field = 1, background = 0)  # any spruce beetle polygon of any host or year, so a living cell was never marked
  fl <- sf::st_read(gdb, quiet = TRUE, query = "SELECT SURVEY_YEAR, Shape FROM SURVEYED_AREAS_FLAT_AllYears_AK_Rgn10 WHERE SURVEY_YEAR BETWEEN 2016 AND 2024")
  flown <- terra::rasterize(terra::vect(fl), r, field = 1, background = 0)  # the ground the surveyors flew over in those years
  con <- terra::project(terra::crop(conifer, terra::project(terra::as.polygons(terra::ext(r), crs = "EPSG:3338"), terra::crs(conifer))), r, method = "average")
  inb <- terra::rasterize(terra::vect(bor), r, field = 1, background = 0); strip <- terra::rasterize(terra::project(terra::as.polygons(terra::ext(sev), crs = "EPSG:32605"), "EPSG:3338"), r, field = 1, background = 0)
  ok <- which(terra::values(inb)[, 1] == 1 & terra::values(strip)[, 1] == 0 & terra::values(flown)[, 1] == 1 & terra::values(con)[, 1] >= 5)  # conifer top cover of 5 per cent or more, flown, inside the borough and outside the severity strip
  v <- data.frame(cell = ok, year = terra::values(year)[ok, 1], pct = terra::values(pct)[ok, 1], marked = terra::values(any_sb)[ok, 1], conifer = terra::values(con)[ok, 1])
  set.seed(seed); dead <- v[sample(which(!is.na(v$year)), min(n, sum(!is.na(v$year)))), ]; dead$dist <- 0
  living <- v[sample(which(v$marked == 0), min(4 * n, sum(v$marked == 0))), ]  # drawn four times over, then kept only within reach of a white spruce polygon
  pts <- sf::st_as_sf(data.frame(terra::xyFromCell(r, living$cell)), coords = c("x", "y"), crs = 3338)
  living$dist <- as.numeric(sf::st_distance(pts, ws[sf::st_nearest_feature(pts, ws), ], by_element = TRUE)); living <- head(living[living$dist <= reach, ], n)
  smp <- rbind(dead, living); smp[, c("x", "y")] <- terra::xyFromCell(r, smp$cell); ll <- sf::st_coordinates(sf::st_transform(sf::st_as_sf(smp, coords = c("x", "y"), crs = 3338), 4326)); smp$lon <- ll[, 1]; smp$lat <- ll[, 2]; smp <- smp[order(round(smp$x / 20000), smp$y), ]  # sorted into 20 km columns, so that one request touches few image tiles
  smp <- cbind(smp, pull_cells(smp, prefix, img = img)); write.csv(smp, csv, row.names = FALSE); smp }
ms <- region_sample("02170", "02.inputs/derived/matsu_sample.csv")
```

```{r}
#| label: matsu-test
#| echo: true
#| output: false
ms$dead <- !is.na(ms$year); ms$arctic[!is.na(ms$arctic) & ms$arctic <= 0] <- NA
ms <- cbind(ms, height_eth = ms$eth, height_glo = ms$glo - ms$dtm, height_arctic = ms$arctic - ms$dtm, HV_2007 = 10 * log10(ms$HV_2007), HH_2007 = 10 * log10(ms$HH_2007), HV_2015 = 10 * log10(ms$HV_2015), HH_2015 = 10 * log10(ms$HH_2015))[, -match(c("HV_2007", "HH_2007", "HV_2015", "HH_2015"), names(ms))]
ms_vars <- c("height_eth", "height_glo", "height_arctic", "HV_2007", "HH_2007", "HV_2015", "HH_2015", "VV65", "VV131")
ms_names <- c(height_eth = "ETH canopy height", height_glo = "the GLO-30 surface minus terrain", height_arctic = "the ArcticDEM surface minus terrain", HV_2007 = "L-band HV of 2007 to 2010", HH_2007 = "L-band HH of 2007 to 2010", HV_2015 = "L-band HV of 2015 and 2016", HH_2015 = "L-band HH of 2015 and 2016", VV65 = "the ascending C-band level", VV131 = "the descending C-band level")  # the sources as the text names them
matsu <- sapply(ms_vars, function(v) { x <- ms[[v]]; ok <- !is.na(x); sev_ok <- ok & (ms$pct >= 20 | !ms$dead); edge <- ok & (ms$dead | ms$dist >= 500)  # every cell, then only the polygons of a fifth or more mortality, then only the living cells at least 500 m from a polygon edge
  c(n = sum(ok), AUC = auc_ok(x, ms$dead), AUC_severe = auc(x[sev_ok], ms$dead[sev_ok]), AUC_edge = auc(x[edge], ms$dead[edge]), dead = mean(x[ok & ms$dead]), living = mean(x[ok & !ms$dead]), rho_pct = cor(x[ok], ms$pct[ok], method = "spearman")) })
dm <- na.omit(ms[, c("dead", "height_eth", "height_glo", "HV_2007", "HH_2007", "VV65", "VV131")])
ms_added <- sapply(list(height = dead ~ height_eth + height_glo, c_band = dead ~ VV65 + VV131, l_band = dead ~ HV_2007 + HH_2007, c_band_height = dead ~ VV65 + VV131 + height_eth + height_glo, l_band_height = dead ~ HV_2007 + HH_2007 + height_eth + height_glo, all = dead ~ VV65 + VV131 + HV_2007 + HH_2007 + height_eth + height_glo),
  function(f) auc(predict(glm(f, family = binomial, data = dm)), dm$dead))  # the same six fits as the strip, on the cells with every source
ms_year <- with(ms[ms$dead, ], sapply(list(height_eth = height_eth, height_glo = height_glo, height_arctic = height_arctic, HV_2007 = HV_2007), function(x) tapply(x, year, mean, na.rm = TRUE)))  # the stands first attacked in each year, by their height before the outbreak
ms_year_n <- table(ms$year[ms$dead]); ms_trend <- with(ms[ms$dead, ], sapply(list(height_eth = height_eth, height_glo = height_glo, height_arctic = height_arctic, HV_2007 = HV_2007), function(x) cor(x, year, method = "spearman", use = "complete.obs")))
```

```{r}
#| label: statewide-regions
#| echo: true
#| output: false
pooled_region <- lapply(names(regions), function(nm) region_sample(regions[[nm]], sprintf("02.inputs/derived/statewide_%s.csv", nm), img = pooled, prefix = paste0("pooled_", nm), n = 5000))  # five thousand dead and five thousand living cells of each region, or every cell where fewer exist
names(pooled_region) <- names(regions)
region_auc <- sapply(pooled_region, function(s) { s$dead <- !is.na(s$year)
  c(dead = sum(s$dead), living = sum(!s$dead), AUC_VV = auc_ok(s$VV, s$dead), AUC_height = auc_ok(s$height, s$dead), VV_dead = mean(s$VV[s$dead], na.rm = TRUE), VV_living = mean(s$VV[!s$dead], na.rm = TRUE), height_dead = mean(s$height[s$dead], na.rm = TRUE), height_living = mean(s$height[!s$dead], na.rm = TRUE),
    above_dead = mean(s$VV[s$dead] >= pooled_strip["thr_VV"], na.rm = TRUE), above_living = mean(s$VV[!s$dead] >= pooled_strip["thr_VV"], na.rm = TRUE),  # the share of each class the strip's threshold calls susceptible
    rho_year_height = if (sum(s$dead) >= 30) cor(s$height[s$dead], s$year[s$dead], method = "spearman", use = "complete.obs") else NA, years = length(unique(s$year[s$dead]))) })
write.csv(region_auc, "03.outputs/statewide_regions.csv")  # read by the abstract, which renders before this chunk
```

The second hypothesis was tested against the aerial detection survey, the only label beyond the strip, in the four regions of @fig-study. In each region, a 90 m grid was laid on the Alaska Albers projection, and the survey's spruce beetle polygons on white spruce of 2016 to 2024 gave each cell its first year inside a polygon and the highest mortality class recorded over it. A cell was dead if it lay inside such a polygon and had conifer top cover of 5 per cent or more, and living if it had that cover, lay inside the ground flown in those years, had never lain inside a spruce beetle polygon of any host or year, and lay within 10 km of a white spruce polygon, so that the living class held forest the beetle could have reached and the surveyors had seen. The cells of the severity map were excluded. In each region, 5 000 dead and 5 000 living cells were drawn at random with a fixed seed, or every cell where fewer existed, and scored by the area under the curve and by the share of each class at or above the strip's threshold. Spearman's rank correlation between the year a dead cell was first recorded and its canopy height tested whether the beetle moved from taller to shorter stands, as @Werner_1983 recorded on the Kenai Peninsula and @Massey_1954 on the White River. In the Matanuska-Susitna Borough, the nine single sources of the strip, with the PALSAR mosaics of 2007 to 2010 that predate every damage polygon, were also read at `r format(sum(ms$dead), big.mark = " ")` dead and `r format(sum(!ms$dead), big.mark = " ")` living cells drawn the same way, and scored again with the dead cells restricted to polygons of 20 per cent mortality or more, to measure the ceiling the survey label set on any source.

## Ground plots

```{r}
#| label: fia
#| echo: true
#| output: false
# USFS Forest Inventory and Analysis DataMart, Alaska PLOT and TREE tables as CSV, plot coordinates published fuzzed by up to about a mile (row `fia-alaska/` of 02.inputs/README.md).
# https://apps.fs.usda.gov/fia/datamart/CSV/AK_PLOT.zip and https://apps.fs.usda.gov/fia/datamart/CSV/AK_TREE.zip
fia_dir <- "02.inputs/fia-alaska"; dir.create(fia_dir, showWarnings = FALSE)
for (t in c("PLOT", "TREE")) if (!file.exists(file.path(fia_dir, paste0("AK_", t, ".csv")))) { z <- file.path(fia_dir, paste0("AK_", t, ".zip")); options(timeout = 600)
  download.file(paste0("https://apps.fs.usda.gov/fia/datamart/CSV/AK_", t, ".zip"), z, mode = "wb", quiet = TRUE); unzip(z, exdir = fia_dir); unlink(z) }
fia_region <- function(counties, csv) {  # one row per forested plot of the named boroughs at its latest measurement, the white spruce tallied on it, and the satellite height at its published coordinate
  if (file.exists(csv)) return(read.csv(csv, colClasses = c(CN = "character")))
  pl <- read.csv(file.path(fia_dir, "AK_PLOT.csv"), colClasses = c(CN = "character")); pl <- pl[pl$COUNTYCD %in% counties & pl$PLOT_STATUS_CD == 1, ]
  pl <- pl[order(-pl$MEASYEAR), ]; pl <- pl[!duplicated(paste(pl$COUNTYCD, pl$PLOT)), ]  # a remeasured plot enters once, at its latest visit
  tr <- read.csv(file.path(fia_dir, "AK_TREE.csv"), colClasses = c(PLT_CN = "character")); ws <- tr[tr$PLT_CN %in% pl$CN & tr$SPCD == 94 & tr$STATUSCD %in% 1:2 & !is.na(tr$DIA), ]  # every live or standing dead white spruce tallied with a diameter; the Kenai remeasurements carry 699 dead trees tallied without one
  ba <- function(d, tpa) sum(pi * (d * 0.0127)^2 * tpa * 2.471, na.rm = TRUE)  # basal area in square metres per hectare from diameter in inches and trees per acre
  f <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(ws, ws$PLT_CN), function(w) { dd <- w$STATUSCD == 2; data.frame(CN = w$PLT_CN[1], n_ws = nrow(w), n_dead = sum(dd), ba_ws = ba(w$DIA, w$TPA_UNADJ), dead_share = ba(w$DIA[dd], w$TPA_UNADJ[dd]) / ba(w$DIA, w$TPA_UNADJ),
    ht_live = mean(w$HT[!dd]) * 0.3048, ht_dead = mean(w$HT[dd]) * 0.3048, ht_max = max(w$HT) * 0.3048, dia_live = mean(w$DIA[!dd]) * 2.54, dia_dead = mean(w$DIA[dd]) * 2.54,
    beetle = sum(!dd & (w$DAMAGE_AGENT_CD1 %in% 11009 | w$DAMAGE_AGENT_CD2 %in% 11009 | w$DAMAGE_AGENT_CD3 %in% 11009)), recent = sum(dd & w$DECAYCD %in% 1:2)) }))  # live trees carrying the survey's spruce beetle code 11009, and dead trees still holding their bark and fine branches
  f <- cbind(f, pl[match(f$CN, pl$CN), c("MEASYEAR", "LAT", "LON")]); names(f)[match(c("LAT", "LON"), names(f))] <- c("lat", "lon"); f$cell <- seq_len(nrow(f))
  near <- pull_cells(f, paste0("fia_cell_", counties[1])); wide <- pull_cells(f, paste0("fia_800m_", counties[1]), buffer = 800); names(wide) <- paste0(names(wide), "_800m")  # the 90 m cell at the published coordinate, and the mean of the cells within 800 m of it, the fuzzing distance
  f <- cbind(f, near, wide); write.csv(f, csv, row.names = FALSE); f }
fia_regions <- list(matsu = fia_region(170, "02.inputs/derived/fia_matsu.csv"), kenai = fia_region(122, "02.inputs/derived/fia_kenai.csv"),  # Matanuska-Susitna and Kenai Peninsula boroughs
  copper = fia_region(261, "02.inputs/derived/fia_copper.csv"), interior = fia_region(c(68, 90, 240, 290), "02.inputs/derived/fia_interior.csv"))  # Valdez-Cordova, and Denali, Fairbanks North Star, Southeast Fairbanks and Yukon-Koyukuk of the Interior, measured in 2014 to 2019 before the outbreak's front entered the Denali Borough
```

```{r}
#| label: fia-test
#| echo: true
#| output: false
fia_regions <- lapply(fia_regions, function(f) { for (s in c("", "_800m")) { f[[paste0("height_glo", s)]] <- f[[paste0("glo", s)]] - f[[paste0("dtm", s)]]; f[[paste0("HV_2007", s)]] <- 10 * log10(f[[paste0("HV_2007", s)]]) }; f })
fia_ground <- sapply(fia_regions, function(f) { b <- f[f$n_dead > 0 & f$n_dead < f$n_ws, ]  # the plots holding both live and dead white spruce
  c(plots = nrow(f), from = min(f$MEASYEAR), to = max(f$MEASYEAR), both = nrow(b), dia_dead = mean(b$dia_dead), dia_live = mean(b$dia_live), ht_dead = mean(b$ht_dead), ht_live = mean(b$ht_live),
    V_dia = unname(wilcox.test(b$dia_dead, b$dia_live, paired = TRUE)$statistic), p_dia = wilcox.test(b$dia_dead, b$dia_live, paired = TRUE)$p.value,  # within one plot, were the trees that died the larger ones
    V_ht = unname(wilcox.test(b$ht_dead, b$ht_live, paired = TRUE)$statistic), p_ht = wilcox.test(b$ht_dead, b$ht_live, paired = TRUE)$p.value,
    dead_share = mean(f$dead_share), half_dead = sum(f$dead_share >= 0.5), beetle_plots = sum(f$beetle > 0), recent = sum(f$recent) / sum(f$n_dead),
    rho_share_ht = cor(f$dead_share, f$ht_max, method = "spearman", use = "complete.obs"), AUC_ht_half = auc_ok(f$ht_max, f$dead_share >= 0.5)) })  # across plots, did the taller white spruce stands lose the larger share
sat <- function(f, v, s = "_800m") { x <- f[[paste0(v, s)]]; ok <- !is.na(x); if (sum(ok) < 30) return(c(n = sum(ok), rho_ht = NA, AUC_half = NA))
  c(n = sum(ok), rho_ht = cor(x[ok], f$ht_max[ok], method = "spearman"), AUC_half = auc(x[ok], f$dead_share[ok] >= 0.5)) }  # the satellite height around the published coordinate against the plot's own tallest tree and its dead share
fia_remote <- sapply(fia_regions, function(f) unlist(lapply(c(eth = "eth", height_glo = "height_glo", HV_2007 = "HV_2007", VV65 = "VV65"), function(v) sat(f, v))))
fia_fuzz <- sapply(c(eth = "eth", height_glo = "height_glo", HV_2007 = "HV_2007", VV65 = "VV65"), function(v) c(cell = sat(fia_regions$matsu, v, "")[["AUC_half"]], m800 = sat(fia_regions$matsu, v)[["AUC_half"]]))  # the Mat-Su cell at the coordinate against the 800 m mean
pfmt <- function(p) if (p < 0.001) "p < 0.001" else sprintf("p = %.3f", p)  # the p-value as the text prints it
write.csv(fia_ground, "03.outputs/fia_ground.csv")  # read by the abstract, which renders before this chunk
```

The second hypothesis was checked on the ground against the public Forest Inventory and Analysis plots of Alaska [@Bechtold_2005], comparing the dead with the live white spruce of each plot as the plot studies compared killed and surviving trees [@Werner_1983; @Doak_2004]. Every forested plot of the four regions was taken at its latest measurement, `r fia_ground["plots", "matsu"]` plots with white spruce in the Matanuska-Susitna Borough (measured `r fia_ground["from", "matsu"]` to `r fia_ground["to", "matsu"]`), `r fia_ground["plots", "kenai"]` on the Kenai Peninsula (`r fia_ground["from", "kenai"]` to `r fia_ground["to", "kenai"]`), `r fia_ground["plots", "copper"]` in the Valdez-Cordova census area (`r fia_ground["from", "copper"]` to `r fia_ground["to", "copper"]`) and `r fia_ground["plots", "interior"]` in the Interior with the Yukon-Koyukuk area added (`r fia_ground["from", "interior"]` to `r fia_ground["to", "interior"]`). The Interior plots were measured before the survey recorded the outbreak's front along the Nenana River, `r sprintf("%.1f", 100 * mean(pooled_region$interior$year[!is.na(pooled_region$interior$year)] >= 2020))` per cent of whose cells it first recorded in 2020 or later, so they stood for white spruce the beetle had not yet reached. The inventory records the diameter and height of every live or standing dead tree and a decay class for the dead, but no cause or year of death. On the plots holding both live and dead white spruce, the mean diameter and height of the dead trees were set against those of the live trees with a paired Wilcoxon signed-rank test. Across all plots, the height of the tallest tree was correlated with the share of white spruce basal area dead and ranked the plots with at least half of that basal area dead by the area under the curve. The radar and height sources were read at each plot's published coordinate, which the inventory shifts by up to about 1.6 km, for the 90 m cell holding it and as the mean of the cells within 800 m.

# Results

## Stand validation

At the 90 m stand scale, on `r sum(sacc$dead[sacc$design == "VV_2014" & sacc$set == "training"], sacc$alive[sacc$design == "VV_2014" & sacc$set == "training"])` training stands labelled dead (`r sacc$dead[sacc$design == "VV_2014" & sacc$set == "training"]`) or living forest (`r sacc$alive[sacc$design == "VV_2014" & sacc$set == "training"]`), the mean VV level of October 2014 to December 2016, before the outbreak reached the areas, ranked the stands the outbreak would kill above the living stands with an area under the curve of `r sprintf("%.2f", change$auc_pre[change$band == "VV131"])` on the descending orbit and `r sprintf("%.2f", change$auc_pre[change$band == "VV65"])` on the ascending (@tbl-validation). The dead stands were `r sprintf("%.1f", with(chg[chg$labelled & chg$band == "VV131", ], mean(pre[dead]) - mean(pre[!dead])))` dB brighter before the outbreak. The change from that level to June 2019 to August 2021 separated nothing, an area under the curve of `r sprintf("%.2f", change$auc_change[change$band == "VV131"])` to `r sprintf("%.2f", max(change$auc_change))`, with the dead stands changing by `r sprintf("%.2f", change$change_dead[change$band == "VV131"])` dB against `r sprintf("%.2f", change$change_alive[change$band == "VV131"])` dB for the living [Welch t-test, t(`r sprintf("%.0f", change$df[change$band == "VV131"])`) = `r sprintf("%.2f", change$t[change$band == "VV131"])`, `r pfmt(change$p[change$band == "VV131"])`]. Conifer cover alone gave `r sprintf("%.2f", change$auc_conifer[1])`, so the pre-outbreak brightness was not canopy density. The network trained on the full monthly series reached an F1 score of `r sprintf("%.2f", sacc$F1[sacc$design == "VV_2014" & sacc$set == "training"])` and an area under the curve of `r sprintf("%.2f", sacc$AUC[sacc$design == "VV_2014" & sacc$set == "training"])` on held-out folds. Its root mean square error was `r sprintf("%.2f", dnet_fit$RMSE_train)` on its own training stands against `r sprintf("%.2f", dnet_fit$RMSE_test)` on the held-out folds, a ratio of `r sprintf("%.2f", dnet_fit$ratio)` above the 1.1 line of @Murphy_2026, so the network was overfitted. The untrained mean of one band matched it at `r sprintf("%.2f", max(unlist(sbase)))`, so the level alone was carried forward.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-validation
#| echo: true
#| tbl-cap: "Area under the receiver operating characteristic curve for ranking the stands the outbreak killed above the living stands, by source and by label. The crown labels are the 90 m stand cells of the Zwieback et al. (2024) training areas, the severity map their 90 m map of 2021, and the survey the aerial detection survey polygons of 2016 to 2024 across the rest of the Matanuska-Susitna Borough. The statewide product is the pooled, angle-corrected VV level of every scene; the two orbits are the single-orbit levels of the same months."
vt <- data.frame(Source = c("Sentinel-1 VV, statewide product", "Sentinel-1 VV, ascending orbit 65", "Sentinel-1 VV, descending orbit 131", "ETH canopy height 2020", "GLO-30 surface minus terrain", "ArcticDEM surface minus terrain", "PALSAR L-band HV", "Conifer top cover"),
  `Crown labels` = c(NA, change$auc_pre[change$band == "VV65"], change$auc_pre[change$band == "VV131"], NA, NA, NA, NA, change$auc_conifer[1]),
  `Severity map` = c(pooled_strip["AUC"], struct["AUC", "VV65_pre"], struct["AUC", "VV131_pre"], struct["AUC", "height_eth"], struct["AUC", "height_glo"], struct["AUC", "height_arctic"], struct["AUC", "HV_pre"], NA),
  `Survey, Matanuska-Susitna` = c(NA, matsu["AUC", "VV65"], matsu["AUC", "VV131"], matsu["AUC", "height_eth"], matsu["AUC", "height_glo"], matsu["AUC", "height_arctic"], matsu["AUC", "HV_2015"], NA), check.names = FALSE)
vt[, -1] <- lapply(vt[, -1], function(x) ifelse(is.na(x), "", sprintf("%.2f", x)))
fmt_tbl(vt)
```

## Landscape validation

Across the `r format(nrow(land), big.mark = " ")` cells of the severity map, `r format(sum(dead_l[lab_l]), big.mark = " ")` dead and `r format(sum(!dead_l[lab_l]), big.mark = " ")` living forest, the pre-outbreak VV level ranked dead above living with an area under the curve of `r sprintf("%.2f", land_auc["level", "VV65"])` on the ascending orbit and `r sprintf("%.2f", land_auc["level", "VV131"])` on the descending. Its rank correlation with severity over every forest cell was `r sprintf("%.2f", land_auc["rho", "VV65"])` and `r sprintf("%.2f", land_auc["rho", "VV131"])` on the two orbits, respectively, and the mean level rose with every severity bin from `r sprintf("%.2f", land_bins["0"])` dB at zero to `r sprintf("%.2f", land_bins["0.1 to 1"])` dB at 0.1 or more on the descending orbit, while the change between the two periods gave `r sprintf("%.2f", land_auc["change", "VV65"])` and `r sprintf("%.2f", land_auc["change", "VV131"])` on the same orbits. The three canopy heights ranked the cells as well as the radar did, the ETH Zurich height at `r sprintf("%.2f", struct["AUC", "height_eth"])`, with mean height of `r sprintf("%.1f", struct["dead", "height_eth"])` m for the dead cells against `r sprintf("%.1f", struct["alive", "height_eth"])` m for the living, the GLO-30 surface minus terrain at `r sprintf("%.2f", struct["AUC", "height_glo"])` and the ArcticDEM surface minus terrain at `r sprintf("%.2f", struct["AUC", "height_arctic"])`. L-band HV of 2015 and 2016 gave `r sprintf("%.2f", struct["AUC", "HV_pre"])`, and height and the C-band level were correlated over the forest cells [Spearman's rho `r sprintf("%.2f", struct["rho_VV65", "height_eth"])`]. On the `r format(nrow(d), big.mark = " ")` cells with every source, logistic fits gave an area under the curve of `r sprintf("%.3f", added["height"])` for height alone, `r sprintf("%.3f", added["c_band"])` for C-band alone, and `r sprintf("%.3f", added["all"])` for all three together. Within every LANDFIRE class with at least 100 cells of each kind, height ranked dead above living, with areas under the curve from `r sprintf("%.2f", min(cover[, "AUC_height"], na.rm = TRUE))` to `r sprintf("%.2f", max(cover[, "AUC_height"], na.rm = TRUE))`, and in Alaska Sub-boreal White Spruce Forest, the one white spruce class with enough cells, height gave `r sprintf("%.2f", cover["Alaska Sub-boreal White Spruce Forest", "AUC_height"])`, with mean height of `r sprintf("%.1f", cover["Alaska Sub-boreal White Spruce Forest", "height_dead"])` m for the dead cells against `r sprintf("%.1f", cover["Alaska Sub-boreal White Spruce Forest", "height_living"])` m for the living, while logistic fits gave `r sprintf("%.3f", cover_added["class"])` for the class alone and `r sprintf("%.3f", cover_added["class_height"])` for class and height together.

No single source reached a separability of M = 1 on the severity map, the index running from `r sprintf("%.2f", min(dsev$M))` for `r dsev$source[which.min(dsev$M)]` to `r sprintf("%.2f", max(dsev$M))` for `r dsev$source[which.max(dsev$M)]`, though every source separated the two classes [Wilcoxon rank-sum, p < 0.001] (@tbl-diagnostics). At their Youden thresholds the sources classed `r sprintf("%.0f", 100 * min(dsev$OA))` to `r sprintf("%.0f", 100 * max(dsev$OA))` per cent of the labelled cells correctly, with Cohen's kappa of `r sprintf("%.2f", min(dsev$kappa))` to `r sprintf("%.2f", max(dsev$kappa))`, and the commission error of the dead class stayed below `r sprintf("%.0f", 100 * max(dsev$com_dead))` per cent while that of the smaller living class ran from `r sprintf("%.0f", 100 * min(dsev$com_living))` to `r sprintf("%.0f", 100 * max(dsev$com_living))` per cent. The logistic fits reached Nagelkerke's R² of `r sprintf("%.2f", min(dfit$R2))` to `r sprintf("%.2f", max(dfit$R2))`, Brier scores of `r sprintf("%.3f", min(dfit$Brier))` to `r sprintf("%.3f", max(dfit$Brier))`, and root mean square errors of `r sprintf("%.2f", min(dfit$RMSE))` to `r sprintf("%.2f", max(dfit$RMSE))` against a mean label of `r sprintf("%.2f", mean(dead_l[lab_l]))`, `r sprintf("%.1f", min(dfit$rRMSE))` to `r sprintf("%.1f", max(dfit$rRMSE))` per cent of that mean, with mean absolute errors of `r sprintf("%.2f", min(dfit$MAE))` to `r sprintf("%.2f", max(dfit$MAE))`, Theil's U bias shares of `r sprintf("%.3f", min(dfit$U_bias))` to `r sprintf("%.3f", max(dfit$U_bias))`, and ratios of held-out to training error of `r sprintf("%.3f", min(dfit$ratio))` to `r sprintf("%.3f", max(dfit$ratio))`, so none was overfitted, while the Hosmer-Lemeshow test rejected the calibration of every fit and the residuals were clustered in space [Moran's I `r sprintf("%.2f", min(dfit$I))` to `r sprintf("%.2f", max(dfit$I))`, p < 0.001; Durbin-Watson `r sprintf("%.2f", min(dfit$DW))` to `r sprintf("%.2f", max(dfit$DW))`] (@tbl-fit).

```{r}
#| label: tbl-diagnostics
#| echo: true
#| tbl-cap: "Separability and classification accuracy of each source at its own Youden threshold against the dead and living cells of the severity map, and of the temporal network at a probability of 0.5 on the held-out folds of the crown labels. M is the separability index of Kaufman and Remer (1994), the difference of the class means over the sum of their standard deviations, starred by the Wilcoxon rank-sum test; AUC is the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve with the 95 per cent confidence interval of DeLong et al. (1988); the threshold is in the source's own unit, decibels for radar, metres for height and probability for the network; κ is Cohen's kappa; commission and omission errors are given for each class; OA is the overall accuracy with its exact binomial 95 per cent confidence interval. * p ≤ 0.05, ** p ≤ 0.01, *** p ≤ 0.001, **** p ≤ 0.0001."
ds <- diag_sep; f2 <- function(x) ifelse(is.na(x), "", sprintf("%.2f", x))
dt <- data.frame(Source = ds$source, Dead = format(ds$dead, big.mark = ","), Living = format(ds$living, big.mark = ","), M = ifelse(is.na(ds$M), "", paste0(f2(ds$M), stars(ds$p_M))), `AUC (95% CI)` = sprintf("%.2f (%.2f, %.2f)", ds$AUC, ds$AUC_lo, ds$AUC_hi), Threshold = f2(ds$thr), κ = f2(ds$kappa),
  `Commission dead` = f2(ds$com_dead), `Commission living` = f2(ds$com_living), `Omission dead` = f2(ds$om_dead), `Omission living` = f2(ds$om_living), `OA (95% CI)` = sprintf("%.2f (%.2f, %.2f)", ds$OA, ds$OA_lo, ds$OA_hi), check.names = FALSE)
fmt_tbl(dt)
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-fit
#| echo: true
#| tbl-cap: "Fit and overfitting diagnostics of the logistic fits of the dead and living cells of the severity map on each source and combination, and of the temporal network on the crown labels. R² is Nagelkerke's, starred by the likelihood ratio test against the null fit; HL is the Hosmer-Lemeshow statistic over ten groups, starred by its test; Brier is the mean squared error of the fitted probability against the label, RMSE its root, rRMSE the root relative to the mean of the label in per cent and MAE the mean absolute error; the RMSE ratio is the root mean square error of the held-out folds over that of the training folds across five spatial folds, 1.1 being the line above which a fit is overfitted (Murphy et al. 2026); U bias is the bias share of Theil's U on the held-out predictions; I is Moran's I of the residuals over the eight nearest cells, starred by its test; DW is the Durbin-Watson statistic of the residuals in cell order. * p ≤ 0.05, ** p ≤ 0.01, *** p ≤ 0.001, **** p ≤ 0.0001."
df <- diag_fit
ft <- data.frame(Model = df$model, n = format(df$n, big.mark = ","), `R²` = ifelse(is.na(df$R2), "", paste0(sprintf("%.3f", df$R2), stars(df$p_R2))), HL = ifelse(is.na(df$HL), "", paste0(sprintf("%.0f", df$HL), stars(df$p_HL))), Brier = sprintf("%.3f", df$Brier), RMSE = sprintf("%.3f", df$RMSE), `rRMSE (%)` = sprintf("%.1f", df$rRMSE), MAE = sprintf("%.3f", df$MAE),
  `RMSE ratio` = sprintf("%.2f", df$ratio), `U bias` = sprintf("%.3f", df$U_bias), I = paste0(sprintf("%.3f", df$I), stars(df$p_I)), DW = sprintf("%.2f", df$DW), check.names = FALSE)
fmt_tbl(ft)
```

```{r}
#| label: statewide-map

state_tif <- "02.inputs/derived/statewide_1km.tif"
if (!file.exists(state_tif)) {  # the exported asset read back at 1 km for the figure and the area table, once the export has finished
  task <- read.csv(task_csv)
  repeat { st <- ee$data$getTaskStatus(task$task)[[1]]$state; if (st == "COMPLETED") break; if (st %in% c("FAILED", "CANCELLED")) stop("export ", st); Sys.sleep(120) }
  a90 <- ee$Image(asset_id)$divide(100)  # the asset is masked where the 90 m cell holds no forest, so VV, scenes and height average over forest cells and the forest share is unmasked to zero before it is averaged, or the share would run high
  img <- ee$Image$cat(list(a90$select(list("VV", "scenes", "height")), a90$select("forest")$unmask(0)))$reduceResolution(ee$Reducer$mean(), maxPixels = 256L)  # 90 m cells averaged into each 1 km cell
  b <- sf::st_bbox(sf::st_transform(sf::st_as_sfc(sf::st_bbox(c(xmin = -170, ymin = 54, xmax = -129, ymax = 71.5), crs = 4326)), 3338)); x0 <- floor(b$xmin / 1000) * 1000; y1 <- ceiling(b$ymax / 1000) * 1000
  nc <- ceiling((b$xmax - x0) / 1000); nr <- ceiling((y1 - b$ymin) / 1000); rows <- split(seq_len(nr), ceiling(seq_len(nr) / 500))
  tile_dir <- "02.inputs/derived/landscape_tiles"
  for (r in rows) { f <- file.path(tile_dir, sprintf("state_%04d.tif", min(r))); if (file.exists(f)) next
    for (attempt in 1:6) { ok <- !inherits(try({ url <- img$getDownloadURL(list(crs = "EPSG:3338", crs_transform = c(1000, 0, x0, 0, -1000, y1 - (min(r) - 1) * 1000), dimensions = c(nc, length(r)), format = "GEO_TIFF", filePerBand = FALSE))
      download.file(url, f, mode = "wb", quiet = TRUE) }, silent = TRUE), "try-error"); if (ok) break; unlink(f); Sys.sleep(30) }
    if (!file.exists(f)) stop("tile ", f, " did not download") }
  terra::writeRaster(terra::merge(terra::sprc(lapply(list.files(tile_dir, "^state_.*\\.tif$", full.names = TRUE), terra::rast))), state_tif) }
alaska_geojson <- "02.inputs/context/alaska_tiger2018.geojson"  # the full-resolution state polygon, for clipping; the 1:20,000,000 outline above is for drawing
if (!file.exists(alaska_geojson)) download.file(ee$FeatureCollection("TIGER/2018/States")$filter(ee$Filter$eq("NAME", "Alaska"))$getDownloadURL("geojson"), alaska_geojson, quiet = TRUE)
state <- terra::mask(terra::rast(state_tif), terra::vect(sf::st_transform(sf::st_read(alaska_geojson, quiet = TRUE), 3338))); names(state) <- c("VV", "scenes", "height", "forest")  # the export rectangle runs east of the border, where the scene search returned nothing, so the map is clipped to the state
vv <- state$VV; vv[state$scenes == 0] <- NA; state$VV <- vv  # a cell no scene covered carries no level
state_area <- do.call(rbind, lapply(c(names(regions), "alaska"), function(nm) {  # square kilometres of forest and of susceptible forest, the forest share of each 1 km cell summed
  v <- if (nm == "alaska") as.data.frame(terra::values(state)) else terra::extract(state, terra::vect(reg_sf[reg_sf$region == nm, ]), ID = FALSE)
  v <- v[!is.na(v$forest) & v$forest > 0, ]
  data.frame(region = nm, forest_km2 = sum(v$forest), susceptible_km2 = sum(v$forest[!is.na(v$VV) & v$VV >= pooled_strip["thr_VV"]]), tall_km2 = sum(v$forest[!is.na(v$height) & v$height >= pooled_strip["thr_height"]]), scenes = median(v$scenes, na.rm = TRUE)) }))
write.csv(state_area, "03.outputs/statewide_area.csv", row.names = FALSE)

```{r}
#| label: statewide-release
#| echo: true
#| output: false
# The release package for managers: the 90 m asset read back whole, clipped to the state, as Cloud Optimized GeoTIFFs with a README, a licence and a QGIS style, zipped for one download from the GitHub release, and the two assets opened to every Earth Engine user. The sources are those of the statewide chunks above.
release_dir <- "03.outputs/release"; release_zip <- file.path(release_dir, "spruce_susceptibility_alaska_90m.zip"); class_asset <- paste0(asset_id, "_class"); class_csv <- "03.outputs/statewide_class_task.csv"
a90 <- ee$Image(asset_id); thr100 <- round(100 * pooled_strip["thr_VV"]); public <- reticulate::dict(readers = list(), writers = list(), all_users_can_read = TRUE)
if (!file.exists(class_csv)) {  # the class map as its own asset: 1 no forest, 2 forest below the threshold, 3 forest at or above it, 4 forest no scene covered, masked outside the state
  cls <- a90$select("forest")$unmask(0)$gt(0)$multiply(ee$Image(1)$add(a90$select("VV")$unmask(0)$gte(thr100))$where(a90$select("scenes")$unmask(0)$eq(0), 3))$add(1)$clip(ak)$rename("class")$toByte()
  task <- ee$batch$Export$image$toAsset(image = cls, description = "spruce_susceptibility_alaska_90m_class", assetId = class_asset, region = ak_box, crs = "EPSG:3338", crsTransform = list(90, 0, 0, 0, -90, 0), maxPixels = 1e10, pyramidingPolicy = list(.default = "mode"))
  task$start(); write.csv(data.frame(task = task$id, asset = class_asset, started = format(Sys.time(), "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M")), class_csv, row.names = FALSE) }
ee$data$setAssetAcl(asset_id, public)  # readable by every Earth Engine user
if (!file.exists(release_zip)) {
  tile_dir <- "02.inputs/derived/release_tiles"; dir.create(tile_dir, showWarnings = FALSE); dir.create(release_dir, showWarnings = FALSE)
  g <- ee$data$getAsset(asset_id)$bands[[1]]$grid; x0 <- g$affineTransform$translateX; y1 <- g$affineTransform$translateY; nc <- g$dimensions$width; nr <- g$dimensions$height  # the asset's own grid
  fetch <- function(img, prefix, step) { for (r in split(seq_len(nr), ceiling(seq_len(nr) / step))) for (cc in split(seq_len(nc), ceiling(seq_len(nc) / step))) {  # square tiles under the 48 MB request limit, each retried
    f <- file.path(tile_dir, sprintf("%s_%05d_%05d.tif", prefix, min(r), min(cc))); if (file.exists(f)) next
    for (attempt in 1:6) { ok <- !inherits(try({ url <- img$getDownloadURL(list(crs = "EPSG:3338", crs_transform = c(90, 0, x0 + (min(cc) - 1) * 90, 0, -90, y1 - (min(r) - 1) * 90), dimensions = c(length(cc), length(r)), format = "GEO_TIFF", filePerBand = FALSE)); download.file(url, f, mode = "wb", quiet = TRUE) }, silent = TRUE), "try-error"); if (ok) break; unlink(f); Sys.sleep(30) }
    if (!file.exists(f)) stop("tile ", f, " did not download") }
    list.files(tile_dir, paste0("^", prefix, "_.*\\.tif$"), full.names = TRUE) }
  full_tiles <- fetch(a90$clip(ak)$unmask(-32768L), "full", 2000L)  # four Int16 bands with their masks, 2,000 by 2,000 cells a request, -32768 where the cell holds no forest or lies outside the state
  repeat { st <- ee$data$getTaskStatus(read.csv(class_csv)$task)[[1]]$state; if (st == "COMPLETED") break; if (st %in% c("FAILED", "CANCELLED")) stop("class export ", st); Sys.sleep(120) }
  ee$data$setAssetAcl(class_asset, public)
  class_tiles <- fetch(ee$Image(class_asset)$unmask(0L, FALSE), "class", 4800L)  # one Byte band read from the finished asset, 0 outside the state, which the download declares as no data
  full_tif <- file.path(release_dir, "spruce_susceptibility_alaska_90m.tif"); class_tif <- file.path(release_dir, "spruce_susceptibility_alaska_90m_class.tif")
  vrt <- file.path(tile_dir, "full.vrt"); sf::gdal_utils("buildvrt", full_tiles, vrt, quiet = TRUE)
  x <- readLines(vrt); for (i in 1:4) x <- sub(sprintf('(<VRTRasterBand dataType="Int16" band="%d"[^>]*>)', i), sprintf("\\1<Description>%s</Description><Scale>0.01</Scale><Offset>0</Offset>", c("VV", "scenes", "height", "forest")[i]), x); writeLines(x, vrt)  # band names and the 0.01 scale factor, carried into the GeoTIFF
  sf::gdal_utils("translate", vrt, full_tif, options = c("-of", "COG", "-co", "COMPRESS=DEFLATE", "-co", "PREDICTOR=2", "-co", "RESAMPLING=AVERAGE", "-co", "BIGTIFF=IF_SAFER", "-co", "NUM_THREADS=ALL_CPUS"), quiet = TRUE)
  cvrt <- file.path(tile_dir, "class.vrt"); sf::gdal_utils("buildvrt", class_tiles, cvrt, options = c("-srcnodata", "0", "-vrtnodata", "0"), quiet = TRUE)
  cl <- terra::rast(cvrt); levels(cl) <- data.frame(id = 1:4, class = c("no forest", "forest below threshold", "susceptible", "forest, no radar scene")); terra::coltab(cl) <- data.frame(value = 1:4, col = c("#f0f0f0", "#a1d99b", "#d7301f", "#9e9ac8"))
  terra::writeRaster(cl, class_tif, filetype = "COG", datatype = "INT1U", NAflag = 0, gdal = c("COMPRESS=DEFLATE", "RESAMPLING=NEAREST", "BIGTIFF=IF_SAFER", "NUM_THREADS=ALL_CPUS"), overwrite = TRUE)
  fill <- function(txt, vals) { for (k in names(vals)) txt <- gsub(paste0("{{", k, "}}"), vals[[k]], txt, fixed = TRUE); txt }  # the README from its template, every number from the saved tables
  share <- function(nm) sprintf("%.0f", 100 * state_area$susceptible_km2[state_area$region == nm] / state_area$forest_km2[state_area$region == nm])
  vals <- list(date = format(Sys.Date(), "%d %B %Y"), thr = sprintf("%.2f", pooled_strip["thr_VV"]), thr100 = sprintf("%d", thr100), thr_height = sprintf("%.1f", pooled_strip["thr_height"]), n_dead = format(pooled_strip["n_dead"], big.mark = " "), n_alive = format(pooled_strip["n_alive"], big.mark = " "),
    sens = sprintf("%.0f", 100 * pooled_strip["sens_VV"]), spec = sprintf("%.0f", 100 * pooled_strip["spec_VV"]), oa = sprintf("%.0f", 100 * pooled_strip["acc_VV"]), auc = sprintf("%.2f", pooled_strip["AUC"]), kappa = sprintf("%.2f", dsev$kappa[dsev$source == "Sentinel-1 VV, statewide product"]),
    auc_kenai = sprintf("%.2f", region_auc["AUC_VV", "kenai"]), auc_matsu = sprintf("%.2f", region_auc["AUC_VV", "matsu"]), auc_copper = sprintf("%.2f", region_auc["AUC_VV", "copper"]), auc_interior = sprintf("%.2f", region_auc["AUC_VV", "interior"]),
    forest_km2 = format(round(state_area$forest_km2[state_area$region == "alaska"]), big.mark = " "), susc_pct = share("alaska"), kenai_pct = share("kenai"), matsu_pct = share("matsu"), copper_pct = share("copper"), interior_pct = share("interior"),
    scenes = sprintf("%d", pooled_strip["scenes"]), angle_slope = sprintf("%.3f", angle_slope), ncol = format(nc, big.mark = " "), nrow = format(nr, big.mark = " "), x0 = format(x0, big.mark = " "), y1 = format(y1, big.mark = " "), size_full = sprintf("%.0f", file.size(full_tif) / 1e6), size_class = sprintf("%.0f", file.size(class_tif) / 1e6),
    asset = asset_id, class_asset = class_asset, release_url = "https://github.com/seamusrobertmurphy/alaska-spruce-beetle-susceptibility-map/releases/tag/map-v1.0")
  writeLines(fill(readLines(file.path(release_dir, "README_template.md")), vals), file.path(release_dir, "README.md"))
  files <- c(full_tif, class_tif, paste0(class_tif, ".aux.xml"), file.path(release_dir, c("spruce_susceptibility_alaska_90m_class.qml", "README.md", "LICENSE.txt"))); files <- files[file.exists(files)]
  utils::zip(release_zip, files, flags = "-j -0") }  # one archive, the GeoTIFFs stored without a second compression

Cells with less than a fifth of their area in forest are blank. Black outlines are the four test regions and the blue frame the validation strip."

Alt text: Two maps of Alaska at 1 km. The left map shades the forest cells by their pre-outbreak Sentinel-1 VV backscatter and the right map by their ETH canopy height of 2020, with the four test regions outlined in black and the validation strip framed in blue.

The pooled product, read on the `r format(pooled_strip["n"], big.mark = " ")` labelled cells of the severity map from a median of `r pooled_strip["scenes"]` scenes per cell, ranked dead above living with an area under the curve of `r sprintf("%.2f", pooled_strip["AUC"])`, with mean VV of `r sprintf("%.2f", pooled_strip["dead"])` dB for the dead cells against `r sprintf("%.2f", pooled_strip["alive"])` dB for the living. Its rank correlation with ETH Zurich height over the forest cells was `r sprintf("%.2f", pooled_strip["rho_height"])`. At the threshold of `r sprintf("%.2f", pooled_strip["thr_VV"])` dB, it called `r sprintf("%.0f", 100 * pooled_strip["sens_VV"])` per cent of the dead cells and `r sprintf("%.0f", 100 * (1 - pooled_strip["spec_VV"]))` per cent of the living cells susceptible, an overall accuracy of `r sprintf("%.0f", 100 * pooled_strip["acc_VV"])` per cent. Against the survey polygons on the same cells it gave `r sprintf("%.2f", pooled_strip["AUC_survey"])`. Across Alaska (@fig-statewide), the map covered `r format(round(state_area$forest_km2[state_area$region == "alaska"]), big.mark = " ")` km² of forest, `r sprintf("%.0f", 100 * state_area$susceptible_km2[state_area$region == "alaska"] / state_area$forest_km2[state_area$region == "alaska"])` per cent of it at or above the threshold. The share ranged from `r sprintf("%.0f", 100 * min(with(state_area[state_area$region != "alaska", ], susceptible_km2 / forest_km2)))` per cent in the `r region_names[state_area$region[state_area$region != "alaska"]][which.min(with(state_area[state_area$region != "alaska", ], susceptible_km2 / forest_km2))]` region to `r sprintf("%.0f", 100 * max(with(state_area[state_area$region != "alaska", ], susceptible_km2 / forest_km2)))` per cent in the `r region_names[state_area$region[state_area$region != "alaska"]][which.max(with(state_area[state_area$region != "alaska", ], susceptible_km2 / forest_km2))]` region (@tbl-area).
